name: vidiq_coach_message_create
title: Send Coach Message
description:
Send a text message from the creator to their assigned human vidIQ coach, in their existing vidIQ coaching chat. A real person reads it, and it cannot be taken back from here. Call this only after showing the creator the exact text, links included, and getting their explicit yes to sending it; if they change the text, show it again. The tool ends every message with a line naming the assistant it came through, such as 'Sent via Claude': tell the creator when you show the draft. Never send on your own initiative, and never add the AI conversation or analytics unless the creator put them in the text.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history. These messages are private: state only the intent in general terms, such as 'send a message to my coach'. Never include the message's content, the coach's words or name, or anything else personal from the conversation.

text.description: The exact message the creator approved, links included; it is sent exactly as given, followed by one line the tool adds itself, such as 'Sent via Claude', so do not write that line into the text. The added line does not count toward the message limit. Standard Coaching plans allow 750 characters per message and other plans may allow more; an over-limit draft is refused with an error that gives the creator's own limit when the coaching chat states it, and otherwise the standard 750. Never split a longer draft.

idempotencyKey.description: A UUID you generate; it keeps a retry from sending the message twice. Generate a new one for every newly approved message, even if its text repeats an earlier one. Reuse an earlier idempotencyKey, with identical text, only to retry this same send after an error that says to.

status.description: The coaching chat accepted the message.

messageId.description: The coaching chat's ID for the message. A retry under the same idempotencyKey returns the same ID.

sentAt.description: When the coaching chat accepted the message (ISO 8601, UTC). A receipt for an earlier send keeps that send's time.

note.description: What this receipt confirms: this call's delivery, or an earlier one matched by idempotencyKey, with nothing new sent.

name: vidiq_coach_message_list
title: List Coach Messages
description:
Read creator-visible messages from the creator's conversation with their assigned human vidIQ coach, latest page first. Call it only when the creator asks about their coach or their coaching messages. Never call it to gather background for other work, such as planning videos, diagnosing a video or a routine account check: most accounts have no human coach, and the call fails for them. Reading does not mark messages read or prove the creator read them. It works whether or not the creator may currently send messages to the coach.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history. These messages are private: state only the intent in general terms, such as 'read my coach's replies'. Never include the message's content, the coach's words or name, or anything else personal from the conversation.

view.description: 'received' (default): the coach's side only, automated messages included. 'conversation': both sides, the creator's own messages included.

cursor.description: olderCursor from the previous page of the same view, for older messages. Omit it for the latest page, then keep passing each page's olderCursor until it is null.

limit.description: Messages per page, 1-50 (default 20). A page can hold fewer, or none, before the end.

note.description: How to read and quote this page, and whether older messages remain.

messageId.description: The coaching chat's ID for the message.

author.description: 'You' for the creator's own messages; otherwise the coach's display name (a previous coach's for older messages), or 'Coach' when it has none.

sentAt.description: When the message was sent (ISO 8601, UTC).

text.description: The message as written; empty for an attachment-only message.

type.description: The attachment's kind, such as 'image', 'video', 'audio' or 'file'; other values can appear.

attachments.description: Attachments by kind only, with no links: the creator opens them in the vidIQ coaching chat.

automated.description: true for a message the chat sent by itself, such as the coach's automatic intro or a system notice; false for one a person wrote.

olderCursor.description: Pass as cursor for older messages. Non-null means more history may remain, even after a short or empty page; null means this page reaches the start of the conversation.

name: vidiq_generate_video_chapters
title: Generate Video Chapters
description:
Start precise YouTube chapter generation from a video's timestamped captions.

Use this when the user wants chapter timestamps, a video outline with exact boundaries, or a chapter block for a YouTube description. The work runs asynchronously: this tool returns a job handle, and `vidiq_job_poll` returns three title alternatives per completed chapter. It requires an accessible transcript and does not update the YouTube video.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID or URL (watch, youtu.be, Shorts, embed, or live URL). The video must have an accessible transcript.

chapterCount.description: Requested chapter count from 4 to 12. Omit to choose automatically from the video duration, normally 4 to 7 chapters.

language.description: Preferred transcript and chapter-title language, such as en or pt-BR.

startBufferSeconds.description: Seconds to move each non-initial chapter earlier so transitions do not feel clipped. Defaults to 2; use 0 for exact caption boundaries.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

name: vidiq_keyword_research
title: Keyword Research
description:
YouTube keyword research: search volume, competition, related/long-tail/question keywords, country rankings, rising trends. Use for all YouTube search queries. Returns keyword metrics, NOT videos (for videos use vidiq_outliers or vidiq_trending_videos).

Choose `mode` by intent:
- `research` (default): measure a phrase and find related keywords, with each row's top countries.
- `matching_terms`: long-tail variations that keep every seed word.
- `questions`: question searches (any/en/es/pt/ru/sv; otherwise matching_terms). For trending or fastest-growing questions set `sort='trending'`.
- `country_search`: a topic's keywords in one country (`keyword` + `country`).
- `country_top`: a country's top searches with no topic (`country` only).
- `rising`: keywords with growing search demand. Scope a subject with free-text `niche` or a channel with `channelId` (only one); use `topic` only when the user asks for a category from `availableTopics`. Omit `language` unless the user asks for one or writes in one; it defaults to the connected channel's language, else en. Rows include top countries and, when available, video views per hour (VPH). For a country, use `language='all'` and keep rows whose `topMarkets` lists it; `country` does not filter rising.
- `rising_vph`: keywords whose videos' views per hour are spiking (video momentum, not search). Offer it after rising; call only if the user wants it (charged separately).

Responses include `Note:` lines on how to read the returned fields; follow and relay them.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

mode.description: Kind of research; see the tool description.

keyword.description: Seed keyword, e.g. 'minecraft tips'. Required for research, questions, matching_terms and country_search.

topic.description: Rising only: a category from a previous rising response's `availableTopics`, only when the user asks for a category. Prefer niche.

includeRelated.description: Research only: include related keyword suggestions (default true).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. 'US'. Required for country_top and country_search; in research adds in-country volume. Does not filter rising.

limit.description: Max rows; use the user's requested count. rising/rising_vph: default 100, max 1000 (100 with niche/channelId). Other modes: default 20, max 100.

sort.description: questions/matching_terms: 'volume' (default) or 'trending' for trending or growing searches. rising/rising_vph: 'growth' (default) or 'relevance' (needs niche or channelId).

broad.description: country_search only: true adds semantically related keywords for a wider list.

language.description: questions: any, en, es, pt, ru, sv (default en). rising/rising_vph: all, en, es, ko, de, hi, ar, th, pl, it, ja, fr, tr, ru, pt, uk. Omit unless the user asks for a language or writes in one: omitted rising, rising_vph and questions use the connected channel's language, else en; a channelId that is not one of the user's connected channels sends none. Use all (any for questions) for every language. A country is not a language.

minVolume.description: research, questions, matching_terms, rising, country_top, country_search: minimum searches, not the 0-100 volume score. Country modes filter in-country volume. Questions/matching_terms/rising filter indexed demand before ranking; displayed estimates may differ. Research filters hydrated monthly searches.

minGrowthPct.description: rising, rising_vph: minimum growth in percent (50 means +50%); rising_vph allows negatives.

includeKeyword.description: Rising only: keep keywords containing this whole word or phrase.

excludeKeyword.description: Rising only: drop keywords containing this whole word or phrase.

maxWords.description: research, questions, matching_terms, rising: max words per keyword.

maxCompetition.description: research, questions, matching_terms, rising: maximum competition score, 0-100 (lower is easier).

niche.description: rising/rising_vph: free-text subject; prefer over topic. Use one of niche, channelId or topic.

channelId.description: rising/rising_vph: YouTube channel ID (UC…, not a handle).

include.description: rising_vph only: up to 20 words/phrases; keep keywords matching any.

exclude.description: rising_vph only: up to 20 words/phrases; drop keywords matching any.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_youtube_video_idea
title: YouTube Video Idea
description:
Call this first, before outliers, trending or keyword research, when the user asks for a new YouTube video idea or what video to make next. Leverages vidIQ research tools for data-backed ideas that are working on YouTube.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID (UC…) of the user's channel the idea is for. Use vidiq_user_channels if you don't know it.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_outliers
title: Video Outliers
description:
Find viral, breakout, and overperforming YouTube videos — videos getting significantly more views than their channel's average. Use this when someone asks for: viral videos, breakout hits, hidden gems, videos blowing up, or more videos like a specific video. For videos gaining views fastest in absolute terms, use vidiq_trending_videos; this tool measures performance relative to a channel's typical results.

Narrow results with `keyword`, `seedVideoId`, `channelIds` or `trendCategories` (formats such as tier lists or video essays); with none set, it returns a broad outlier feed from the other filters. Leave `publishedWithin` unset unless the user asks for newer or older videos: wider windows match the topic less closely. Each result has a breakout score: its views relative to the channel's typical video. For videos with visually similar thumbnails, use vidiq_similar_thumbnails.

If you can't open the thumbnail links, pass the video IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

keyword.description: Topic the videos should be about. Can be a short topic ("budget travel") or a full concept ("a creator tries living on $1 a day for a week").

requireAllTitleTerms.description: Set true to require every keyword term in the title. Use for names and exact phrases; it can return few results.

seedVideoId.description: A YouTube video to find more videos like: an 11-character video ID (e.g. "dQw4w9WgXcQ") or a video URL. Results cover the same topic from other channels; the seed's own channel is left out. Use instead of `keyword` when the user points at a specific video. Cannot be combined with `keyword` or `requireAllTitleTerms`; other filters apply as usual.

channelIds.description: Channel filter for focusing results on up to 50 specific creators or competitors. Each entry may be a channel ID (UC...), a handle (@MrBeast or MrBeast), or a channel URL — handles and URLs are resolved to channel IDs automatically. May be combined with `keyword`.

contentType.description: "long" for long-form videos (default) or "short" for Shorts.

hasAiLabel.description:
Long-form only. Filters by YouTube's AI label, which also covers partly AI-altered videos (such as AI b-roll), not just fully AI-generated ones.
- unset (default): all videos
- true: only videos confirmed to have the AI label
- false: only videos confirmed to have no AI label
Most videos haven't been checked for the label yet, so true and false return far fewer results. Set it only when the user asks for only, or no, AI-labeled videos.

minEngagementRate.description: Minimum engagement rate (likes/views, 0-1). Filters out low-engagement copycat and re-upload channels: real creators typically show 0.03-0.12, content farms 0.002-0.01. Around 0.02 helps when `seedVideoId` is a mega-viral video.

publishedWithin.description: How far back to search: "thisWeek", "thisMonth", "threeMonths", "sixMonths", "oneYear", "twoYears" or "allTime". Leave unset unless the user asks for newer or older videos. Long-form windows beyond a year, and English Shorts windows beyond 3 months, match the topic less closely.

channelCountry.description: Restrict to channels BASED IN this country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "PL", "US"). This is where the channel/creator is located — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the language of the videos. To search by the content language, use `language` instead. Example: for Polish-language outliers pass `language='pl'`; `channelCountry='PL'` alone only restricts to channels based in Poland (which may publish in any language).

language.description: Return videos whose titles are in this language, as a single ISO 639-1 code. Supported: en, es, ko, de, hi, ar, th, pl, it, ja, fr, tr, ru, pt, uk. Pass a code when the user asks for a language or writes in one; otherwise omit it: it defaults to the connected channel's language, else "en". With `seedVideoId` and no `language`, it follows the seed video's language. With `channelIds` and no `language`, no language filter is applied. Non-English searches cover the last 6 months. For example: Spanish-language outliers → "es"; German breakout videos → "de"; "видео на русском" → "ru". Pass exactly one code; unsupported codes are rejected. Write `keyword` in that language.

trendCategories.description: Filter by video category/format IDs (e.g. reaction, tier_list, mukbang); combine with keyword for the subject. Use vidiq_trend_categories when the appropriate ID is unknown, and reuse IDs already available in context. These are outlier-video categories, not rising-keyword topics.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_similar_thumbnails
title: Similar Thumbnails
description:
Find long-form YouTube videos whose thumbnails LOOK similar — visual/semantic similarity over the thumbnail images themselves. This tool searches long-form videos only; Shorts are not supported. This is not topic, title, or keyword search (for those use vidiq_outliers or vidiq_youtube_search; for videos on the same topic as a given video, use vidiq_outliers with `seedVideoId`). Two modes: pass `description` with a textual description of the imagery (e.g. "a shocked creator pointing at a red analytics chart") to find thumbnails matching that description, or pass `videoId` to find thumbnails that look like that video's thumbnail (resolved automatically — no image upload needed). Useful for thumbnail inspiration, checking how common a thumbnail concept is, or finding which visual styles perform well in a niche.

If you can't open the thumbnail links, pass the video IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

description.description: Natural-language description of the thumbnail imagery to find, e.g. "a shocked creator pointing at a red analytics chart". Provide exactly one of `description` or `videoId`.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or video URL. The video's current thumbnail is resolved automatically and used as the search image. Provide exactly one of `description` or `videoId`.

publishedWithin.description: Filter by publish date. Defaults to any publish date.

channelCountry.description: Restrict to channels BASED IN this country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. 'US', 'PL'). This is where the channel is located — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the language of the videos.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

hasAiLabel.description: Whether the source reports an AI label; null means unknown.

name: vidiq_channel_stats
title: Channel Stats
description:
Measure a YouTube channel's growth over a configurable date range, with subscriber count, total views, video count, and metadata. For current metadata/counts of multiple known channel IDs, batch them with vidiq_get_channels_by_ids instead; do not call both when one result answers the request.

Use this tool to:
- Look up any YouTube channel's current stats (subscribers, views, videos)
- See how much a channel has grown over a given period
- Get channel metadata (country, language, topics, creation date)

If you can't open the avatar links, pass the channel IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

from.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 30 days ago

name: vidiq_trending_videos
title: Trending Videos
description:
Find YouTube videos gaining views rapidly. If the user names a subject, ALWAYS put that subject in titleQuery; selecting a language and a vph or recentVph sort without titleQuery would lose the subject. Omit titleQuery only when the user wants all subjects.

Use this when someone asks: what's trending, what's hot right now, popular videos this week, or fastest-growing videos. Unlike vidiq_outliers (which measures performance vs channel average), trending measures absolute velocity — high VPH regardless of channel size.

Use this tool to discover:
- Videos that are trending right now on YouTube
- Trending content in specific niches via title search
- High-performing videos filtered by views per hour, engagement, or subscriber range

For "right now", "going viral" or "fastest-growing" requests, use sortBy='recentVph': it ranks by views gained in the latest measured hour. Use sortBy='vph' when the user wants the strongest videos over their whole time since publishing, since vph is the lifetime average.

Preserve the requested topic in `titleQuery`, even for fastest-growing searches. For example, fastest-growing gardening videos means titleQuery='gardening' and sortBy='recentVph', not an unfiltered list.

For language-specific discovery, pass the user's requested actual video-title language in `videoTitleLanguage`. Set `videoTitleLanguage='all'` to search across languages. `channelCountry` only restricts where channels are based; it does not represent audience geography or video language.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoFormat.description: Video format: 'long' for regular videos, 'short' for YouTube Shorts

titleQuery.description: The user's requested topic, used for semantic video-title search. Set this whenever the request names a subject or niche, including when sorting by vph or recentVph. Language and sort filters do not preserve the topic. Omit only for topic-unrestricted discovery.

requireAllTitleTerms.description: Tighten titleQuery matching: when true, every term must appear in the title (strict AND), so high-velocity videos matching only a common token (e.g. 'ai') can't dominate. When false (default), titleQuery is a broad relevance signal. Only affects results when titleQuery is set.

channelCountry.description: One country code or a non-empty list of country codes (e.g. ['US', 'GB', 'AU', 'CA']). Restrict to channels BASED IN any of these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. 'US', 'PL'). This is where the channel is located — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the language of the videos. To filter by the video's language, use `videoTitleLanguage` instead.

includeUnknownCountry.description: Only with channelCountry: when true, also return videos from channels that list no country. Many label, studio and publisher channels list none, so a country filter alone drops them. Leave unset to return only channels based in channelCountry.

videoTitleLanguage.description: Filter by detected video-title language (ISO 639-1): en, es, ja, ru, ko, ar, hi, vi, id, th, tr, de, fr, pl, pt, uk, it, mr, or fa. Use all to search across languages. Pass the user's requested content language, or one they write in; otherwise omit it: it defaults to the connected channel's language (all when that language is not listed), else en. This filters language only: also set titleQuery whenever the user names a topic, rather than returning every subject in that language.

videoPublishedAfter.description: Only videos published after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

videoPublishedBefore.description: Only videos published before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

sortBy.description: relevance (default): topical fit when titleQuery is supplied; otherwise falls back to vph. vph: views per hour averaged over the video's whole lifetime; for a named topic, also supply titleQuery so the fastest videos stay on that topic. recentVph: views gained in the latest measured hour, so it ranks what is gaining fastest right now, including older videos that are picking up. recentVphEngaged: recentVph weighted by engagement rate, so fast videos that viewers also like and comment on rank above fast videos with little reaction, such as loops and background streams. viewCount: accumulated views, not current momentum. engagementRate: engagement ratio. videoPublishedAt: newest uploads.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_tiktok_trending_sound_search
title: Search Trending TikTok Sounds
description:
Find TikTok songs and original sounds trending right now, from vidIQ's daily chart of about 400 sounds over the last 14 days, optionally narrowed to a creator's niche. Returns each sound's TikTok link, videos per day, estimated views per hour, growth, and a few popular TikToks using it. Use this when a creator asks which sound or song to use on TikTok, what audio is trending, or which trending sounds suit their niche.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

query.description: The creator's niche or content topic, e.g. 'gym workouts' or 'anime edits'. Keeps only sounds that a meaningful share of their videos use for this kind of content. Omit for the overall chart.

sort.description: 'relevance' ranks by niche match (needs query), 'popular' by estimated views per hour today, 'rising' by growth in daily video count over the window. Defaults to relevance with a query, otherwise popular.

soundType.description: 'song' for licensed tracks with an artist, 'original' for audio uploaded by a TikTok user. Omit for both.

name: vidiq_title_thumbnail_wins
title: Title & Thumbnail Changes That Worked
description:
Find long-form YouTube videos (not Shorts) whose views per hour at least doubled after the creator changed the title, the thumbnail, or both. Use this when the user asks which title or thumbnail changes worked or raised views, for repackaging ideas, or for before/after examples, in a niche or across YouTube. For one video's change log, use `vidiq_video_change_history`. Only videos published in the last 3 months are covered.

Returns up to 10 changes: on the topic with `summary`, or from every niche without it, ordered by `sort`, with low-quality changes left out. For videos outperforming their channel without a packaging change, use `vidiq_outliers`.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

summary.description: The topic or niche only, matched against what each video is about (its content summary), e.g. 'budget meal prep for students' or 'Minecraft'. Not the user's question: leave out words like title, thumbnail, change or worked, which pull in videos about YouTube itself. Omit it for a broad question: one call lists changes from every niche, ordered by `sort`.

sort.description: Highest first: 'changed_at' (newest change, the default without `summary`), 'views_ratio' (biggest lift) or 'vph_before' (most views per hour before the change).

language.description: Return videos whose titles are in this language, as a single ISO 639-1 code. Pass a code when the user asks for a language or writes in one; otherwise omit it: it defaults to the connected channel's language, else "en". For example: Spanish-language videos → "es"; "видео на русском" → "ru".

changeType.description: Only this kind of change: 'title' (title change), 'thumbnail' (thumbnail change) or 'both' (title and thumbnail change). Omit for all.

publishedWithin.description: Only videos published in the last 'month' or '3_months' (default).

changedWithin.description: Only changes made in the last 'month' or '3_months' (default).

vphBeforeMin.description: Minimum views per hour before the change.

viewsRatioMin.description: Minimum after/before views-per-hour ratio. Every result is already at least 2.

subscriberCountMin.description: Minimum current channel subscribers. Channels that hide their count are left out.

subscriberCountMax.description: Maximum current channel subscribers. Channels that hide their count are left out.

viewCountMin.description: Minimum current views of the video.

viewCountMax.description: Maximum current views of the video.

engagementRateMin.description: Minimum engagement rate, (likes + comments) ÷ views as a fraction: 0.005 (0.5%) by default, 0.02 for 2%, 0 for no floor. Videos with hidden likes are always kept.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_channel_search
title: Channel Search
description:
Search YouTube channels by niche or topic (natural-language `query`, semantic + lexical) and structured filters. For viral-video discovery, use vidiq_outliers.

For COMPETITORS of a channel — the user's own ("who are my competitors?") or a named one ("channels similar to Creator Insider") — prefer vidiq_similar_channels. If a canonical channel ID is already available, call it directly with channelId and optional size/sort; do not first look up the channel's characteristics here. Use this tool when the reference channel needs identifying, or for generic channel discovery.

Use it to:
- Look up a specific channel by `handle`.
- Require a phrase in the channel `description`.
- Filter by size, recency, format (long/short/mixed), growth and per-format metrics (7d/30d/1y), creation date, country, language, main category, faceless, breakout.
- Find emerging channels: set breakoutChannel: true for any 'breakout / emerging / up-and-coming channels in X' intent.
Combine any inputs; at least one of query, handle, channelTitle, or a filter is required.

Sort: keep the default relevance for topical asks, even 'top/popular/biggest channels about X' (it already favors notable channels); field sorts are ONLY for explicit metric scans.

Language and location (`languages` = what channels publish in; `country` = where they are based, not audience location). Results should match the request's language unless the user says otherwise.
- Never translate: `query` is just the topic, in the user's own words. For a non-English request, also set `languages` to that language.
- A place in the request → set its country and keep the place in the query ('tokyo street food' → ['JP']), except travel/culture coverage, where creators from anywhere qualify.
- News, politics, or local events about a country → always set that country (its own channels, not foreign coverage).
- Local or language-specific discovery: request limit 20+.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

query.description: Free-text query describing the niche, topic, or content (e.g. 'vegan cooking tutorials', 'tech reviews', 'minecraft let's plays'). Drives semantic search across niches and description embeddings plus lexical match on niches/description. Write the query in the LANGUAGE THE USER USED — NEVER translate their wording to English. The search is multilingual; translating discards the language signal and returns the wrong locale's channels. Non-English request → keep the original wording here AND set `languages` to the request's language (e.g. 'дай каналы про уроки макияжа' → query: 'уроки макияжа', languages: ['ru']). Optional — you can also run a pure metrics/attribute search by providing only filters.

channelTitle.description: Optional channel title fragment to bias results toward channels whose title matches (e.g. 'Mark Rober').

channelTitleMatch.description: How to match channelTitle. 'fuzzy' (default) ranks by title similarity (partial matches allowed). 'exact' restricts to channels whose title equals the value (case-insensitive). Requires channelTitle — rejected if set without it.

handle.description: YouTube handle / custom URL (e.g. '@MrBeast' or 'mrbeast'). Leading '@' is optional. Use this when you want a specific channel.

handleMatch.description: How to match handle. 'exact' (default) returns only the channel with that exact handle. 'fuzzy' does a partial/relevance match (e.g. 'beast' matches '@MrBeast'). Requires handle — rejected if set without it.

description.description: Require a phrase in the channel description: the words must appear consecutively, in order, each tolerating small typos. A hard filter (restricts the result set, works with any sort), unlike `query` which only ranks. Use when the user wants channels whose DESCRIPTION says something specific (e.g. description: 'redstone tutorials' or 'business inquiries'). For topic/niche discovery, prefer `query`.

faceless.description: Filter by faceless-channel status. true returns only faceless channels, false excludes them.

breakoutChannel.description: Filter by breakout-channel flag. true also switches ranking to emerging-channel mode: the popularity prior is disabled so small fast-rising channels rank by pure relevance instead of being outranked by established ones. Use breakoutChannel: true for any 'breakout / emerging / up-and-coming channels in X' intent. Omit to return both breakout and non-breakout channels with default ranking. Replaces the deprecated vidiq_breakout_channels tool.

country.description: Filter by channel country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, uppercase, e.g. ['US', 'GB']): the country where the channel is BASED — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the channel's language (use `languages` to filter by language). Multiple codes are OR-ed. When the query names a place ('tokyo street food', 'nyc daily vlogs'), pass the corresponding country code(s) — e.g. tokyo → ['JP'] — and keep the city name in the query. For news, politics, or local-events queries about a country ('news and politics in Ukraine'), ALWAYS set that country (usually with its language in `languages`): the audience wants that country's channels, not foreign channels covering it. Skip the country filter only for travel/culture coverage intent where creators from anywhere qualify ('travel vlogs about Japan').

languages.description: Filter by the actual language(s) the channels publish content in (ISO 639-1 codes, lowercase, e.g. ['en', 'es']). Always pass the user's requested content/channel language here; this is channel language, NOT channel country. When the USER'S REQUEST is written in a non-English language and does not request a different content language, or they explicitly ask for content in a specific language ('на русском', 'auf deutsch'), pass that actual content language here — e.g. query 'уроки макияжа' → languages: ['ru']. Do not translate the query; the search understands non-English text, but without this filter big channels in other languages will outrank local ones. By default matches any channel that *contains* a requested language (multilingual channels included). Set exactLanguage=true to return only monolingual channels whose language is exactly the requested value.

exactLanguage.description: When true, match languages exactly (only monolingual channels whose single language equals the requested code). Prefer true when the user wants content purely in that language — multilingual channels (e.g. 'hi, en') often produce content mostly in their other language. When false/omitted, match any channel containing the requested language(s). Requires a non-empty `languages` list — rejected if true without it.

mainCategory.description: Filter by main category (YouTube topic labels as stored in the index — e.g. 'Knowledge' for educational content, 'Video game culture' for gaming, 'Lifestyle (sociology)' for lifestyle). Values are case-sensitive and must come from the enum; multiple values are OR-ed.

avgViewsMin.description: Minimum lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos). Use for 'averages 100k+ views per video'. This is the per-video average, not total views.

avgViewsMax.description: Maximum lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos). Use for 'averages under 10k views a video'.

estimatedEarningsMin.description: Minimum estimated MONTHLY channel earnings in USD. Hard filter: channels with unknown earnings are excluded. Use for 'channels earning over $10k a month'.

estimatedEarningsMax.description: Maximum estimated MONTHLY channel earnings in USD. Hard filter: channels with unknown earnings are excluded. Use for 'channels making under $1000 a month'.

longAvgDuration7dMin.description: Minimum average long-form video duration over the trailing 7 days (seconds).

longAvgDuration7dMax.description: Maximum average long-form video duration over the trailing 7 days (seconds).

longAvgDuration30dMin.description: Minimum average long-form video duration over the trailing 30 days (seconds).

longAvgDuration30dMax.description: Maximum average long-form video duration over the trailing 30 days (seconds).

longAvgDuration1yMin.description: Minimum average long-form video duration over the trailing year (seconds).

longAvgDuration1yMax.description: Maximum average long-form video duration over the trailing year (seconds).

shortAvgDuration7dMin.description: Minimum average short-form video duration over the trailing 7 days (seconds).

shortAvgDuration7dMax.description: Maximum average short-form video duration over the trailing 7 days (seconds).

shortAvgDuration30dMin.description: Minimum average short-form video duration over the trailing 30 days (seconds).

shortAvgDuration30dMax.description: Maximum average short-form video duration over the trailing 30 days (seconds).

shortAvgDuration1yMin.description: Minimum average short-form video duration over the trailing year (seconds).

shortAvgDuration1yMax.description: Maximum average short-form video duration over the trailing year (seconds).

longVideoCount7dMin.description: Minimum number of long-form videos published in the trailing 7 days.

longVideoCount7dMax.description: Maximum number of long-form videos published in the trailing 7 days.

longVideoCount30dMin.description: Minimum number of long-form videos published in the trailing 30 days.

longVideoCount30dMax.description: Maximum number of long-form videos published in the trailing 30 days.

longVideoCount1yMin.description: Minimum number of long-form videos published in the trailing year.

longVideoCount1yMax.description: Maximum number of long-form videos published in the trailing year.

shortVideoCount7dMin.description: Minimum number of short-form videos published in the trailing 7 days.

shortVideoCount7dMax.description: Maximum number of short-form videos published in the trailing 7 days.

shortVideoCount30dMin.description: Minimum number of short-form videos published in the trailing 30 days.

shortVideoCount30dMax.description: Maximum number of short-form videos published in the trailing 30 days.

shortVideoCount1yMin.description: Minimum number of short-form videos published in the trailing year.

shortVideoCount1yMax.description: Maximum number of short-form videos published in the trailing year.

longViewCount7dMin.description: Minimum long-form view count accrued in the trailing 7 days.

longViewCount7dMax.description: Maximum long-form view count accrued in the trailing 7 days.

longViewCount30dMin.description: Minimum long-form view count accrued in the trailing 30 days.

longViewCount30dMax.description: Maximum long-form view count accrued in the trailing 30 days.

longViewCount1yMin.description: Minimum long-form view count accrued in the trailing year.

longViewCount1yMax.description: Maximum long-form view count accrued in the trailing year.

shortViewCount7dMin.description: Minimum short-form view count accrued in the trailing 7 days.

shortViewCount7dMax.description: Maximum short-form view count accrued in the trailing 7 days.

shortViewCount30dMin.description: Minimum short-form view count accrued in the trailing 30 days.

shortViewCount30dMax.description: Maximum short-form view count accrued in the trailing 30 days.

shortViewCount1yMin.description: Minimum short-form view count accrued in the trailing year.

shortViewCount1yMax.description: Maximum short-form view count accrued in the trailing year.

publishedAfter.description: Filter by channel creation date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD): created on or after this date.

publishedBefore.description: Filter by channel creation date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD): created on or before this date.

lastVideoPublishedAfter.description: Last uploaded video on or after this date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) — active channels.

lastVideoPublishedBefore.description: Last uploaded video on or before this date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD).

nicheConfidenceMin.description: Minimum niche-classification confidence (0–1). Each channel is tagged with a niche and a confidence score; this floors out low-confidence / likely-misclassified channels so results stay on-topic. Defaults to 0.3 to favor cleanly-classified channels — set to 0 to disable the floor and include unclassified/low-confidence channels.

limit.description: Number of channels to return (max 50). For geo-local or language-specific discovery, request 20+ — relevant local channels may rank below globally popular ones.

sort.description: Result ordering: 'relevance' (default for text searches; ranks by semantic + lexical score), 'subscriberCount' (subscribers desc), 'subsGrowth30d' (30-day subscriber growth desc), 'viewsGrowth30d' (30-day view growth desc), or 'lastVideoPublished' (most recently active first). Pure-filter searches default to subscriberCount desc. Use 'relevance' for ALL topical queries including 'popular/famous/top channels in X' — relevance ranking already favors notable channels. Use field sorts only for explicit metric scans ('most subscribed regardless of topic fit', 'fastest growing') — they re-order by the raw metric, ignoring topical fit; pair growth sorts with subscriberCountMin (e.g. 1000) because growth percentages explode at tiny subscriber bases.

name: vidiq_comment_insights
title: YouTube Comment Insights
description:
Find what a YouTube niche's audience asks for and complains about in comments, or test a video idea against that evidence. Searches indexed comments across a cohort of channels qualified for the niche; for one video's or channel's comments use vidiq_video_comments.

Modes (prefer discover/validate):
- discover: recurring audience requests and pain points, with thread/channel counts and quoted evidence.
- validate (needs idea): a verdict on one idea, separating direct from adjacent evidence.
- raw: ranked comment threads, only when the underlying comments are needed. Continue with ONLY mode="raw" and cursor (free).

Async: returns an `mcpJobId`; poll `vidiq_job_poll` until completed. Failed or expired jobs, and searches where no comments match, are refunded.

Pass niche and idea in English (the channel taxonomy is English-only) and the audience language in `language`. Omit commentPublishedAfter unless the user asks for a time boundary. Raw-only fields are rejected with discover/validate.

Completed results include `notes` on how to read them; follow and relay them.

Cost: 5 credits per discover, validate, or new raw search. Raw cursor pages are free.

mode.description: discover: audience requests and pain points. validate: test one idea. raw: ranked comment threads for your own analysis; pages run up to ~10k tokens, so delegate clustering to a subagent if your host supports it.

niche.description: YouTube niche or topic in English (translate, e.g. 'cocina' -> 'cooking'); selects the channel cohort. Not a channel handle or URL. Required except on raw cursor pages.

idea.description: validate only: the video idea to test, in English. It must add something beyond the niche.

language.description: Two-letter language of the audience comments (e.g. 'pl'); omit for all languages. The audience language goes here, not in niche.

commentPublishedAfter.description: Only comments posted on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO datetime), including on older videos. Set only when the user asks for a time boundary.

includeReplies.description: New raw searches only. Include viewer replies; creator replies are always excluded.

intents.description: New raw searches only. Keep comments carrying any of these 1-5 intent labels.

minLikes.description: New raw searches only. Minimum comment like count.

sort.description: New raw searches only. relevance to the niche (default), likes, or newest.

pageSize.description: New raw searches only. Maximum threads per page (1-50); pages are byte-bounded and usually hold 10-15.

maxThreadsPerChannel.description: New raw searches only. Maximum threads from one channel per page (default 5, 0 = no limit).

cursor.description: Raw continuation: the previous page's nextCursor. Send only mode='raw' and cursor; free, expires after one hour.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

name: vidiq_video_earnings_estimate
title: Estimate Video Earnings
description:
Estimate a single YouTube video's ad-revenue earnings as a low/mid/high range in USD.

Give it a video id or URL. It resolves whether the video is long-form or a Short, looks up the channel's category and country, and applies vidIQ's RPM model (category RPM x geo multiplier, with a much lower RPM for Shorts).

Use this to answer "how much did/does this video earn?".

Important: this is a rough estimate, not exact. It assumes the channel is monetized, uses the channel's country as a proxy for viewer geography, and counts all views as ad-serving. Channels under ~1,000 subscribers are usually not monetized.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

videoId.description: A YouTube video id (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or any YouTube video URL (watch, youtu.be, /shorts/, /embed/, /live/)

name: vidiq_earnings_calculate
title: Calculate Earnings From Views
description:
Calculate estimated monthly YouTube earnings (low/mid/high USD) for a given number of monthly views.

This is a calculator, not a lookup: it does not fetch anything from YouTube, so you must supply the numbers. Use it for "how much would X views/month earn?", what-if scenarios, and niche/geo comparisons. To price a real, existing video by id or URL, use vidiq_video_earnings_estimate instead.

Set subject to 'video' for one video (then format 'long' or 'short' is required) or 'channel' for a channel's mixed output (then shortsShare is the fraction of views that are Shorts, default 0 = all long-form). Content format and the supplied context can significantly affect the estimate, so provide accurate inputs and ask the user when the format or mix is unknown.

Provide category, country, language, and subscriberCount when known. The result is an estimate, not the channel's actual revenue.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

subject.description: What the monthly views belong to: 'video' (a single video, so it is either long-form or a Short) or 'channel' (a mix, so pass shortsShare)

monthlyViews.description: Monthly views to price (the estimate returned is monthly)

category.description: Content category. Providing the accurate category improves the estimate

format.description: Video format. Required when subject is 'video'; must be omitted when subject is 'channel' (use shortsShare instead). Content format significantly affects the estimate

shortsShare.description: Channel only: fraction of monthly views that are Shorts (0.3 = 30%). Defaults to 0. Content mix significantly affects the estimate

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country of the audience or channel

language.description: Content language. Use an ISO-639-1 code or a locale tag such as en-US

subscriberCount.description: Channel subscriber count, when known. Providing it improves the estimate

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_video_stats
title: Video Stats History
description:
Get historical statistics for a YouTube video over time, including views, likes, comments, and views per hour (VPH).

Use this tool to:
- Track how a video's performance changes over time
- Compare view velocity (VPH) across different periods
- Analyze engagement trends (likes, comments) for a specific video

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

granularity.description: Time granularity for stats data points

from.description: Start of time range as an RFC 3339 timestamp, e.g. '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'

to.description: End of time range as an RFC 3339 timestamp, e.g. '2026-01-31T00:00:00Z'

name: vidiq_video_change_history
title: Video Change History
description:
Get the observed title and thumbnail change history for one YouTube video. Pass a video ID or a YouTube watch, youtu.be, Shorts, or live URL.

Each change records when a title or thumbnail edit was observed. Thumbnail entries include the original YouTube URL and vidIQ's archived snapshot URL. The response also includes observed thumbnail A/B tests and their variants. To find which changes raised views across many videos, use `vidiq_title_thumbnail_wins`.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (for example 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or a YouTube video URL.

name: vidiq_get_videos_by_ids
title: Get Videos by IDs
description:
Get detailed metadata for one or more YouTube videos.

Use this tool to:
- Fetch video details such as title, description, tags, and category
- Get current statistics (views, likes, comments, views per hour (VPH), outlier score and engagement rate) for specific videos. VPH, outlier score and engagement rate are latest values only, not historical observations.
- Look up publishing info, channel details, and thumbnails for videos
- Check topic categories for videos

If you can't open the thumbnail links, pass the video IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoIds.description: One to 50 YouTube video IDs or URLs

vph.description: Latest views per hour. Null means unavailable.

outlierScore.description: Latest outlier multiplier. Null means unavailable.

engagementRate.description: Latest engagement rate as a fraction: 0.06 means 6%. Null means unavailable.

name: vidiq_get_images
title: Get Images
description:
See actual pictures: YouTube thumbnails and avatars, Instagram photos, Reel covers, and carousel slides. For Instagram use kind instagram_media with a post/Reel permalink or shortcode from earlier results; select the 1-based slide (default 1). Repeat a post with different slide numbers to read a carousel in order. Numeric Meta media IDs and CDN image URLs are not accepted. Photos and slides come back as labeled MCP images; a video slide returns its still image, not a video analysis. Private or unavailable public posts may not load. Use it when you need to look at a thumbnail or avatar but the app you run in can't open its image link, for example before you describe, compare or critique them.

Pass each item's kind and its ID, handle or URL exactly as earlier results show it. Each picture comes back after a numbered label; an item that can't be shown is listed with the reason.

To score a thumbnail use vidiq_score_thumbnail; to find look-alike thumbnails use vidiq_similar_thumbnails.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

slide.description: Instagram only: 1-based carousel slide number; defaults to 1. Request multiple items with the same post and different slides to inspect a carousel in order.

kind.description: What the picture belongs to: youtube_video (its thumbnail; a Short returns its vertical cover), youtube_channel (its avatar), thumbnail_snapshot (a thumbnail URL from a vidIQ result, including A/B test variant thumbnails), or instagram_media (a photo, Reel cover, or selected carousel slide).

id.description: The item exactly as it appears in earlier vidIQ results: a YouTube video ID or URL, a channel ID (UC…), @handle or channel URL, or a thumbnail URL. For Instagram, pass the post/Reel permalink or shortcode; never a numeric Meta media ID or CDN image URL.

items.description: Pictures to show, in the order you want them. Up to 10, or 3 at "full" resolution.

resolution.description: "preview": up to 640 px, enough for composition, faces, colors and large text. "full": up to 1280 px, for reading small text or inspecting fine detail; at most 3 items.

name: vidiq_youtube_preview
title: Preview on YouTube
description:
Use when the user wants to see how a long-form video's thumbnail and title look on YouTube: desktop Home and Search, a thumbnail Gallery, and the mobile app, beside real long-form competitors. Not for Shorts. A title and thumbnail are required unless videoId is given. The widget has a Copy image button the user can paste back into chat for feedback.

Cost: 1 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

title.description: Required unless videoId is given. Title to preview on your video card. With videoId, it overrides the video's current title; leave it out to keep that title.

thumbnailUrl.description: One of thumbnailUrl or thumbnailFile is required unless videoId is given. Thumbnail to preview as an image URL: a generated or refined thumbnail's imageUrl, a YouTube thumbnail, or any other image link. Use thumbnailFile instead for an image the user attached or uploaded. With videoId, it overrides the video's current thumbnail; leave both thumbnail fields out to keep that thumbnail.

thumbnailFile.description: One of thumbnailUrl or thumbnailFile is required unless videoId is given. Thumbnail to preview from the user's vidIQ image library, as the imageId from vidiq_file_upload. For an image attached in chat or on the user's device, open vidiq_file_upload so the user can upload it. With videoId, it overrides the video's current thumbnail; leave both thumbnail fields out to keep that thumbnail.

searchQuery.description: The short phrase a viewer would type into YouTube search to find this video, e.g. 'diy garage workshop'. Home and Search competitors are both matched to it.

language.description: The title's language as an ISO 639-1 code, so competitors match it. Defaults to English.

channel.description: Optional channel to show on the user's card: a channel ID, @handle or URL. Defaults to the video's channel, then the user's connected channel.

videoId.description: Optional existing YouTube video ID or URL. The card shows its real views, publication date and duration, and its current title and thumbnail unless title or a thumbnail field overrides them.

channel.description: Channel name shown on the user's card.

language.description: Language the competitors were matched to.

name: vidiq_youtube_search
title: Search YouTube
description:
Search all of YouTube for videos, channels, or playlists matching a query, with optional filters (topic, region, publish date, duration, channel). Use this when someone asks to "find videos about X", "search YouTube for Y", "find channels about Z", or wants results for a specific keyword.

Unlike vidiq_trending_videos (which returns what's hot right now) and vidiq_outliers (which finds videos over-performing relative to their channel), this is a general keyword search across the whole catalog. It returns raw YouTube search results, NOT keyword metrics — for search volume/competition use keyword research instead.

Use this tool to:
- Find videos, channels, or playlists by keyword (set 'type')
- Narrow results by topic, region, publish-date window, and (for videos) duration, definition (HD), or live/upcoming event type
- Search within a single channel by passing 'channelId'
- Sort by relevance, recency ('date'), or popularity ('viewCount')

Filters marked "Video only" require type='video'.

If you can't open the thumbnail or avatar links, pass the video or channel IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

type.description: Kinds of result to return — any combination of video, channel, playlist. Defaults to all three. The video-only filters require type to be exactly ['video'].

order.description: Sort order. 'date' = newest, 'viewCount' = most viewed, 'videoCount' = channels with most videos.

publishedAfter.description: Only results published after this RFC 3339 timestamp, e.g. '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'

publishedBefore.description: Only results published before this RFC 3339 timestamp, e.g. '2026-02-01T00:00:00Z'

channelId.description: Restrict the search to a channel ID, @handle, or YouTube channel URL

regionCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code to localize results (e.g. 'US', 'DE')

videoDuration.description: Length: short (<4min), medium (4-20min), long (>20min). Video only.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

id.description: YouTube id of the video, channel, or playlist (depending on kind)

channelId.description: Channel id associated with this result, when available

viewCount.description: Current view count. For videos this is video views; for channels this is total channel views.

videoCount.description: Number of public videos, channel results only

duration.description: Video duration as an ISO 8601 duration, video results only

likeCount.description: Current video likes, video results only

commentCount.description: Current video comments, video results only

subscriberCount.description: Subscriber count for the result's channel, when public and available

vph.description: Views per hour from vidiq outlier/trend data, video results only

outlierScore.description: Outlier score from vidiq outlier data, video results only

name: vidiq_get_channels_by_ids
title: Get Channels by IDs
description:
Fetch current metadata and counts for known YouTube channel IDs. Batch multiple IDs in one call. For a channel's growth over a date range, use vidiq_channel_stats instead; do not call both when the current snapshot answers the request.

Use this tool to:
- Look up channel metadata (title, description, country) for one or more channels
- Get subscriber counts, view counts, and video counts
- Retrieve channel tags and topic categories
- Check channel thumbnails

If you can't open the avatar links, pass the channel IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelIds.description: List of YouTube channel IDs to look up

name: vidiq_balance
title: Credits Balance
description:
Check the user's current vidIQ credits balance.

vidIQ credits live in two buckets:
- A renewable bucket sized by the user's plan (Free/Boost/Max/etc) that refills each billing cycle.
- Zero or more add-on (bonus) credits. Add-on credits drain alongside renewable credits but do NOT refill.

Field semantics are in the output schema. Key invariant: totalCredits = renewableCredits + addOnCredits; maxRenewableCredits is the plan cap only.

Example — Boost user with an open promo grant:
  { type: 'limited', totalCredits: 1800,
    renewableCredits: 1500, maxRenewableCredits: 2000,
    renewableResetsAt: '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z',
    addOnCredits: 300, maxAddOnCredits: 500 }
Read as: 1,800 left = 1,500 of 2,000 renewable + 300 of a 500-credit bonus pool. Renews Jun 1.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

type.description: 'limited' means the user has a finite renewable credit budget that refills each billing cycle. 'unlimited' means the user is on an unlimited plan (e.g. enterprise) and the renewable bucket does not decrement.

totalCredits.description: Total remaining credits the user can spend right now — renewableCredits plus addOnCredits. Null when type='unlimited'. This is the headline number to show in chat.

renewableCredits.description: Remaining credits in the renewable plan bucket alone — does NOT include add-on credits. Null when type='unlimited'.

maxRenewableCredits.description: The user's renewable plan cap (e.g. 150 for Free, 2000 for Boost, 6000 for Max). This is the amount that refills each billing cycle. Does NOT include add-on credits. Null when the plan has no cap.

renewableResetsAt.description: ISO timestamp when the renewable credit bucket next renews. Add-on credits do NOT renew; only the renewable bucket. Null when type='unlimited' or the backend did not return a renewal time.

addOnCredits.description: Remaining add-on (bonus) credits. Drain alongside renewable credits and do NOT refill on the billing cycle.

maxAddOnCredits.description: Initial total of all currently-active add-on credits — i.e. how much bonus credit the user originally received. Combine with addOnCredits to compute add-on usage.

name: vidiq_user_channels
title: User Channels
description:
Get the list of YouTube channels authorized by the current user.

Each channel includes its `title`, `handle`, `subscriberCount`, `viewCount` and
`videoCount`, so there is no need to call vidiq_get_channels_by_ids for the listed
channels' names or current counts. Any of these fields is null when the value is
unavailable (no handle, hidden subscriber count, or metadata that could not be loaded);
refer to such a channel by its ID instead of guessing a name or number.

The response includes `authenticatedAs` (the email of the connected vidIQ account).
An empty `channels` list usually means the user authorized a different account than
they expected — tell them which account they're connected as and suggest reconnecting
with the intended one rather than treating it as an error.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

title.description: Channel title, or null when YouTube metadata could not be loaded.

handle.description: YouTube handle including the leading @, or null when the channel has no handle or its metadata could not be loaded.

subscriberCount.description: Current subscriber count, or null when the channel hides it or its metadata could not be loaded.

viewCount.description: Lifetime view count, or null when it could not be loaded.

videoCount.description: Number of public videos, or null when it could not be loaded.

authenticatedAs.description: Email of the vidIQ account this MCP connection is authenticated as. When the channel list looks wrong or empty, surface this so the user can confirm they connected the intended account.

name: vidiq_user_videos
title: User Videos
description:
List videos from one of the current user's directly authorized YouTube channels through the authenticated vidIQ MCP connection, including public, unlisted, and private videos.

Use vidiq_user_channels when the channel ID is unknown. Supports privacy, video-type, title-search, ordering, limit, and cursor filters. Set privacyStatus to exactly the requested statuses; do not include public videos in a private/unlisted-only search. Use vidiq_channel_videos for arbitrary public channels. Do not fall back to public results when channel authorization fails.

If you can't open the thumbnail links, pass the video IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

channelId.description: Canonical YouTube channel ID owned by the current user. Call vidiq_user_channels if unknown.

privacyStatus.description: Return only these privacy statuses. Match the user's requested statuses exactly: private or unlisted means ['private', 'unlisted'], without public. Omit only when all statuses are acceptable; the default includes public, unlisted, and private videos.

videoType.description: Video type filters. Omit when all long, short, and live videos are acceptable.

search.description: Optional title-only search string, from 1 to 100 characters.

pageToken.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous call with the same filters.

name: vidiq_channel_videos
title: Channel Videos
description:
Get videos from a known YouTube channel by format (long-form, Shorts, or live streams). For recent/latest uploads, set popular=false (default); for most-popular uploads, set popular=true. To discover videos across many channels, use vidiq_outliers or vidiq_trending_videos.

Use vidiq_user_videos instead when the user needs their owned-channel library, private or unlisted videos, title search, privacy filters, or cursor pagination.

Use this tool to:
- Browse a channel's recent uploads by video type (popular=false, default)
- Discover a channel's most popular videos by type (popular=true)
- Compare current views, likes, comments, views per hour (VPH), and breakout scores
- Get video metadata including titles, publish dates, thumbnails, and durations

For "audit my channel", an own-channel review, or explaining why the user's channel or videos are underperforming or growing, call vidiq_youtube_channel_audit first once the channel is identified. This also applies after the user chooses a channel for an audit. Use this upload list only for a requested list or a follow-up to the audit.

If you can't open the thumbnail links, pass the video IDs to vidiq_get_images.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

videoFormat.description: Type of videos to retrieve: 'long' for long-form, 'short' for Shorts, 'live' for live streams

popular.description: For recent/latest uploads, pass false (default). For most-popular uploads, pass true. This selects the upload list, not a date-range filter.

channelThumbnail.description: YouTube channel avatar thumbnail URL, or null if unavailable

viewCount.description: Current YouTube view count, or null if unavailable

likeCount.description: Current YouTube like count, or null if unavailable

commentCount.description: Current YouTube comment count, or null if unavailable

duration.description: Video duration in ISO-8601 format (for example, 'PT12M34S'), or null if unavailable

vph.description: Current views per hour, or null if unavailable

breakoutScore.description: Performance relative to the channel's typical videos, or null if unavailable

name: vidiq_video_transcript
title: Video Transcript
description:
Get the full transcript (captions) of a YouTube video.

Use this tool to:
- Analyze what a video talks about without watching it
- Extract key topics, quotes, or timestamps from a video
- Compare content across multiple videos by reading their transcripts
- Research video content for SEO or content strategy purposes

When a language is requested, this tool never silently substitutes captions in another language.

When there is no transcript, the error says why: the video is live or scheduled (retry after the stream ends), YouTube is still generating captions for a recent upload (retry in a few minutes), the stream has been live for over a day, the video has no captions on YouTube, or the video is private or unavailable. Only retry when the error says to; otherwise tell the user why the transcript is missing.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or a YouTube video URL

language.description: Requested transcript language as a BCP-47 code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'pt-BR'). When supplied, only a matching caption track is returned; omit it to use the video's default captions.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

transcription.description: Caption text in lines of `[m:ss] text` (`[h:mm:ss]` past one hour), where the timestamp is when the line starts.

name: vidiq_video_comments
title: Video Comments
description:
Get YouTube comment threads for a video or channel, including replies.

Provide exactly one of videoId or channelId.

For recurring questions, unmet needs, or video-idea validation across a niche, use vidiq_comment_insights instead of manually collecting many videos' comments. Keep using this tool when the request concerns these specific videos or channels; niche-wide evidence is not a substitute for their comments.

Each returned thread carries the videoId and videoTitle it belongs to, so channel-wide results can be attributed to individual videos. Either field is omitted when YouTube does not report it or the video's metadata is unavailable. Each thread also carries its commentId (the top-level comment) and the channelId that owns the video; byChannelOwner marks comments written by that channel, for example to find threads the creator has not answered yet.

Use this tool to:
- Understand audience sentiment and reactions to a video
- Find common questions or feedback themes in comments
- Browse recent comments across an entire channel
- Identify the most liked or discussed comments

Paging and filtering: maxResult is the upstream page size, and minLikes filters that page by top-level comment likes. A page can therefore come back with fewer threads than maxResult, or with none at all, while more matches still exist. Each page is a separate charged call, so do not sweep to exhaustion by default: fetch another page with the returned nextPageToken (same filters) only while you still need more evidence and the caller's budget allows, and stop as soon as you have enough. A null nextPageToken means the upstream corpus is exhausted and there is nothing left to read.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or video URL. Provide either videoId or channelId.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID, handle (e.g. '@MrBeast'), or channel URL. Provide either videoId or channelId.

maxResult.description: Upstream page size: how many comment threads are fetched per call (1–100). When minLikes is set, fewer threads than this can be returned because filtering is applied to the fetched page only — request another page with nextPageToken if the matches so far are not enough.

minLikes.description: Optional inclusive like threshold on the top-level comment: keep only threads whose top-level comment has at least this many likes. Replies of kept threads are not filtered. Omit (or 0) to return every thread.

pageToken.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's nextPageToken. Pass the same videoId/channelId, order, and minLikes when continuing.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

commentId.description: ID of the top-level comment, which is also the thread ID. Replies to this thread target this ID.

channelId.description: ID of the channel that owns the video. Omitted when YouTube did not report one.

videoId.description: ID of the video this thread belongs to. Omitted when YouTube did not report one.

videoTitle.description: Title of the video this thread belongs to. Omitted when the video's metadata is unavailable (e.g. deleted or private).

byChannelOwner.description: True when the channel that owns the video wrote this comment.
True when the channel that owns the video wrote this comment.

name: vidiq_channel_performance_trends
title: Channel Video Performance Trends
description:
Get a channel's typical video performance curve — how views accumulate over time after publication.

Returns statistical aggregates (min, max, avg, median, percentiles) of view counts at various time intervals since publication, based on the channel's recent videos.

Use this tool to:
- Understand how quickly a channel's videos gain views after publishing
- Compare a channel's view velocity against benchmarks
- Identify whether a channel has strong initial traction or slow-burn growth

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID, handle (e.g. '@MrBeast'), or channel URL

name: vidiq_youtube_channel_audit
title: Audit YouTube Channel
description:
Audit a YouTube channel and open its interactive audit widget. Use for "audit my channel", "review my channel", a channel health check, "how is my channel doing?", "why are my views low?" or "why isn't my channel growing?", including why recent videos are underperforming or stalled. The user does not need to ask for a widget. It compares the channel's last 30 days of private analytics with the 30 before, long-form and Shorts separately, ranks its best and worst recent uploads against its typical views, and adds similar channels and recent breakouts in its niche. Call it before pulling the user's own video lists, stats or transcripts, then look deeper at the videos it names.

It also answers: what to fix first when growth stalls; why views aren't turning into subscribers; Shorts versus long-form; how the channel compares with peers; and monetization progress.

Works on any channel. A channel the user has connected to vidIQ gets the full audit; any other gets only its public half, with no private analytics. If none is named, use vidiq_user_channels: the single connected channel, or ask which when several are connected; with none connected, ask which channel to audit. Once the channel is identified, call this tool directly; an upload list or hand-built analytics report does not replace the audit.

Without a channel diagnosis, use vidiq_channel_analytics for metric totals, period comparisons, rankings or a video's retention curve; vidiq_channel_videos for recent uploads, views rankings or median views; and vidiq_video_stats for named videos' views over time. This tool does not generate assets or publish changes.

Cost: 10 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: A YouTube channel as an ID (UC…), @handle or channel URL.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_channel_analytics
title: Channel Analytics
description:
Get YouTube Studio analytics for the user's connected channel: views, watch time, subscribers, retention, traffic sources, audience and revenue, by day, video, country, device or traffic source.

Use this when the user asks "this week vs last week", "where do viewers drop off", "which videos earn the most" or "Shorts vs long-form". Identify the connected channel with `vidiq_user_channels` first when needed. For another channel's public numbers, use `vidiq_channel_stats`.

For "audit my channel" or why the user's channel isn't growing, call vidiq_youtube_channel_audit once the channel is identified; use this tool for metrics and follow-ups.

Reports whole days. For an hour-aligned window (whole UTC hours, at most 7 days), use a Studio browser report if that tool is available.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

report.description: Named report preset that fills metrics/dimensions/sort with a known-good YouTube Analytics report shape (explicitly-passed metrics/dimensions/sort/maxResults still win). audience_retention: per-video retention curve — REQUIRES filters='video==VIDEO_ID'. traffic_sources: views by source (search, suggested, browse, external...). audience_demographics: age/gender split (viewerPercentage). audience_geography: views by country. revenue_report: daily earnings (monetized channels only; combine with dimensions=['video'] for per-video earnings — YouTube does not support revenue by traffic source). revenue_per_video: own videos ranked by estimated revenue, with views, CPM, playback-based CPM and monetized playbacks, plus the derived rpm column (monetized channels only). top_videos: own videos ranked by views (pass sort='-estimatedRevenue' plus revenue metrics to rank by earnings instead). shorts_vs_longform_split: views/watch-time split between Shorts, long-form and live (creatorContentType).

startDate.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 28 days ago

metrics.description: Metrics to retrieve. Default: views, engagedViews, estimatedMinutesWatched, subscribersGained, likes, comments. Since 2026-08-27 YouTube counts views from the first frame, so views runs about 1.7–1.9× higher than before on long-form; engagedViews is not affected by that change. Use engagedViews for any before/after comparison that spans that date and for outlier judgments on the channel's own videos. Some dimensions support only a restricted metric set — an unsupported metric is rejected, and omitted metrics narrow to the supported subset of the default.
