Each restricted dimension and the metrics it allows: insightTrafficSourceType, insightTrafficSourceDetail, insightPlaybackLocationType, insightPlaybackLocationDetail, deviceType → views, engagedViews, estimatedMinutesWatched, averageViewDuration, averageViewPercentage; subscribedStatus → those plus likes, dislikes, shares, videosAddedToPlaylists, videosRemovedFromPlaylists, annotationClickThroughRate; ageGroup, gender → viewerPercentage; elapsedVideoTimeRatio → audienceWatchRatio, relativeRetentionPerformance, totalSegmentImpressions, startedWatching, stoppedWatching (where viewers start/stop watching per 1% segment; also available as a single-video total with no dimensions and filters='video==VIDEO_ID'). videosAddedToPlaylists and videosRemovedFromPlaylists are not available with creatorContentType, and top-video reports can't be sorted by shares or those playlist metrics (sort by views instead). For subscriber/comment/share metrics use a time/geo dimension (day, country) or video.

dimensions.description: Dimensions to break down by (e.g. day, country, deviceType). month: startDate/endDate are snapped to the first of their month (YouTube requires month-aligned bounds). video, insightTrafficSourceDetail, insightPlaybackLocationDetail are top-N reports (ranked by views; pass sort/maxResults to change); the two *Detail dims also need a parent-type filter (insightTrafficSourceType== / insightPlaybackLocationType==), and those filters are valid only with their matching *Detail dimension. elapsedVideoTimeRatio (audience retention) needs a video== filter. Most dimensions can't be combined (YouTube supports only specific report shapes) — if a combo is rejected, request each dimension separately.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of rows to return. insightTrafficSourceDetail and insightPlaybackLocationDetail allow at most 25 (default 25); video allows at most 200 (default 25); elapsedVideoTimeRatio requires at least 100 (default 100) because audience retention is a 100-point curve and does not have the video's 200-row ceiling.

filters.description: Filter expression (e.g. 'video==dQw4w9WgXcQ', 'country==US', 'creatorContentType==shorts'; content types are shorts, videoOnDemand, liveStream)

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending (e.g. '-views')

name: vidiq_subscriber_insights
title: Subscriber & Commenter Audience Insights
description:
Audience overlap for a YouTube channel: which other channels share its audience. Returns raw, possibly noisy overlap, not a curated competitor list.
- audienceSource="subscribers" (default): for a channel authorized to the user's account. Returns channels its subscribers also subscribe to, with dated overlap history, plus the strongest three-hour posting windows from sampled subscriber activity.
- audienceSource="commenters": for any channel. Returns channels sharing commenters, from a sample of collected comments. No comment text or identities; cannot answer growth or posting-time questions.

For competitors by content similarity use vidiq_similar_channels; for what commenters say use vidiq_video_comments; for tracked competitors use vidiq_list_competitors.

A missing subscriber report starts one on-demand generation (needs a vidIQ OAuth connection). When reportStatus is returned there is no data and no charge: follow nextAction and message, without tight polling. If subscriber data is unavailable, you may offer commenter overlap as a different signal, but never call it automatically. Recommend only; never add or remove tracked competitors unless asked.

Responses include `notes` on how to read the returned fields; follow and relay them.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID, handle, or URL. Subscribers: a channel authorized to your account; commenters: any channel.

audienceSource.description: subscribers (default): subscriber overlap and posting windows for your authorized channel. commenters: sampled shared-commenter peers for any channel.

timezoneOffset.description: Subscribers only: whole-hour UTC offset (Z or ±HH:00) for bestTimeToPost. Ignored for commenters.

limit.description: Max overlap channels: subscribers default 25 (max 50); commenters default 50 (max 100).

period.description: Subscribers: legacy 30_days identifier. Commenters: 90_days describes the publication-age retention window of the collected comment sample, not complete coverage or freshness relative to today.

growthUpdatedAt.description: Present for ready subscriber reports; absent for pending/unavailable reports and commenters. When growth history was updated, or null when unavailable.

topChannels.description: Present for ready subscriber reports (possibly empty); absent for pending/unavailable reports and commenters.

bestTimeToPost.description: Present for ready subscriber reports; absent for pending/unavailable reports and commenters. Timezone-adjusted public activity, not watch history.

audienceSource.description: Required and equal to commenters in commenter mode; omitted in subscriber mode.

commentAudience.description: Required for commenters; absent for subscribers. Shared-commenter peer counts. Missing reports return an empty peer array.

reportStatus.description: Only present when subscriber data is not ready. Pending is not a completed report; unavailable means an existing activity artifact but a missing top-channel report; authorization_required needs an OAuth reconnect. None are charged.

notes.description: How to read the returned fields; follow and relay them. Absent with reportStatus.

name: vidiq_trend_categories
title: Outlier Video Categories
description:
Discover supported video categories and formats for vidiq_outliers, such as tier lists, reactions, and video essays. Use when the user wants to explore supported formats or you need a category ID. Returns category IDs, display names, and descriptions; pass returned IDs into vidiq_outliers.trendCategories. This lists categories, not currently trending videos or rising-keyword topics. Rising keyword topics come from vidiq_keyword_research mode=rising via availableTopics/suggestedTopics. Reuse IDs already available in context; do not call before every search.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

name: vidiq_similar_channels
title: Similar Channels
description:
Find COMPETITORS of a channel — the user's own or a specific named channel — using neural semantic search tuned for competitor matching.

Use ONLY when someone asks for competitors or similar channels relative to a channel:
- "Who are my competitors?", "Find channels like mine" (the user's own channel; niche mode auto-detects country/language)
- "Channels similar to [channel]", "Competitors of [channel]", "Channels like @handle" (a named reference channel)

Do NOT use for generic channel discovery by topic, size, growth, or any other criteria ("find tech review channels", "top gaming channels in Brazil", "fastest growing fitness channels") — use vidiq_channel_search.

Choose exactly one mode: channelId or niche.

CHANNEL ID MODE — when a canonical YouTube channel ID beginning with UC was supplied or already resolved, pass only channelId, plus optional size and sort. Do not add niche or other filters, or copy resolved channel characteristics: the API derives the source classification and search tuning and excludes the reference channel. Do not call vidiq_channel_search when a canonical ID is already available. Handles and URLs are not resolved here; resolve them to a canonical ID first.

LEGACY MANUAL NICHE MODE — niche is required: always a clear topic or content theme. All other filters (marked "Niche mode only") are optional. The user's own authorized channels are excluded automatically; country and language are auto-detected from the user's authorized channel when omitted.

To match a specific reference channel in niche mode, do NOT guess its characteristics: fill niche, country, language, channelType, faceless, minSubscribers/maxSubscribers, avgViews, and excludeChannelIds from its data, as each parameter describes.

Omit sort to keep similarity ranking; set it only when the user asks to rank these competitors by size or recent growth.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

channelId.description: Canonical YouTube channel ID beginning with UC. It is passed directly to the Similar Channels API without a resolution request.

niche.description: Manual niche, topic, or content theme to search in. Use natural language — e.g. 'tech reviews' or 'vegan cooking tutorials'. Provide either this or channelId, not both; prefer channelId for a specific reference channel. When matching a reference channel in niche mode, use its niche + subNiches, comma-separated (e.g. 'YouTube Growth, Monetization & SEO').

minSubscribers.description: Niche mode only. Lower bound for subscriber count. Use to filter out smaller channels — e.g. 10000 to only see channels with 10k+ subscribers. Use together with maxSubscribers to define a specific range. When matching a reference channel in niche mode, set it to roughly 10% of its subscriberCount unless the user asks for a specific range.

maxSubscribers.description: Niche mode only. Upper bound for subscriber count. Use to filter out larger channels — e.g. 1000000 to cap results at channels under 1M subscribers. Use together with minSubscribers to define a specific range. When matching a reference channel in niche mode, set it to roughly 5x its subscriberCount unless the user asks for a specific range.

avgViews.description: Niche mode only. The reference channel's lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos). When searching for competitors of a specific channel, pass its avgViews here so results are auto-ranged to a similar per-video-views league (parallels passing the reference channel's subscriber band); do not also set avgViewsMin/avgViewsMax unless the user asks for a specific range. Leave unset for generic niche searches.

avgViewsMin.description: Niche mode only. Manual lower bound for lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos), overriding the avgViews auto-range. Use to require results that average at least this many views per video — e.g. 50000 for '50k+ average views'. This is the per-video average, not total views. When matching a reference channel, prefer avgViews and set this only when the user asks for a specific range.

avgViewsMax.description: Niche mode only. Manual upper bound for lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos), overriding the avgViews auto-range. Use together with avgViewsMin to define a specific per-video average-views range. When matching a reference channel, prefer avgViews and set this only when the user asks for a specific range.

country.description: Niche mode only. Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code used to prefer channels BASED IN that country — e.g. 'US', 'GB', 'BR', 'JP'. Matching channels receive a ranking boost, but channels based elsewhere may still appear. This is where the channel is located — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the channel's language (use `language` to filter by language). When matching a reference channel in niche mode, use its country. When omitted, the country is auto-detected from the user's authorized channel (if any).

language.description: Niche mode only. Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code to filter results to channels whose content is in that language — e.g. 'en', 'es', 'pt', 'ja'. Pass the user's requested content language here (the language the channel publishes in — this is the channel's language, not its country). Only a single language is accepted. When matching a reference channel in niche mode, use the first code from its languages. When omitted, it defaults to the user's connected channel's language, else 'en'. Pass 'all' to search every language.

channelType.description: Niche mode only. Reference channel format — when matching a reference channel in niche mode, use its channelType. 'long' prefers long and mixed candidates; 'short' prefers short and mixed candidates; 'mixed' is neutral. This affects ranking, not eligibility.

faceless.description: Niche mode only. Reference channel faceless status — when matching a reference channel in niche mode, use its isFaceless value. When provided, candidates with the same status receive a ranking boost; other candidates remain eligible.

sort.description: Optional descending sort of the requested top similarity results: subscriberCount, subsGrowth30d, or viewsGrowth30d. Set only when the user asks to rank these competitors by size or recent growth; any explicit sort reorders only the requested top similarity results. Omit to keep neural similarity relevance order. Results include these metrics plus channelType and isFaceless.

size.description: Number of similar channels to return. Defaults to 30, maximum 50.

excludeChannelIds.description: Niche mode only. Channel IDs to exclude from results. When matching a reference channel, include its channelId. The user's own authorized channels are excluded automatically and do not need to be listed.

name: vidiq_submit_feedback
title: Submit Feedback
description:
Submit feedback about the vidIQ MCP — feature requests, bug reports, improvement suggestions, survey responses, or general comments. When the user encounters a bug with vidIQ MCP or requests a new vidIQ MCP feature, proactively ask whether they would like you to submit a bug report or feature request to vidIQ. Call this tool when the user explicitly asks to submit, send, record, or report feedback to vidIQ. Comments made while asking for help do not by themselves indicate submission intent. If submission intent is ambiguous, ask whether the user wants the feedback sent to vidIQ and wait for confirmation.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

type.description: The kind of feedback: feature_request for new tools/capabilities, bug_report for something broken, improvement for enhancing an existing tool, survey_response for answers to a survey or research invitation, general for anything else

tool_name.description: The relevant existing tool name, if this feedback is about a specific tool (e.g. 'vidiq_keyword_research')

description.description: What you're requesting, reporting, or suggesting — and why

summary.description: Concise, searchable summary of this feedback (up to 500 characters)

campaign_id.description: Survey or campaign identifier provided in the invitation; omit for ordinary feedback

use_case.description: A specific workflow or scenario for additional context

name: vidiq_score_title
title: Score Title
description:
Score a YouTube video title for click-through-rate potential. Returns a score (0-100) indicating how compelling and clickable the title is. Use this to compare title variations and pick the best-performing option. Afterwards, offer vidiq_youtube_preview to show the title beside real YouTube competitors.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID or video URL (improves scoring accuracy)

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID (UC…) or youtube.com/channel/UC… URL (improves scoring accuracy)

name: vidiq_score_thumbnail
title: Score Thumbnail
description:
Score a YouTube video thumbnail for click-through-rate potential. Returns a score (0-100) with detailed feedback on strengths and improvements. Provide a video ID and title; optionally supply a custom thumbnail image URL to score instead of the current YouTube thumbnail. Afterwards, offer vidiq_youtube_preview to show the thumbnail beside real YouTube competitors.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID or video URL

title.description: Video title (used together with the thumbnail for scoring)

image.description: Thumbnail image URL or an uploaded image. If omitted, the current YouTube thumbnail is used.

imageId.description: image as the imageId of a picture in the user's vidIQ image library, as the upload picker or vidiq_upload_image returns it. Send it instead of image.

name: vidiq_generate_titles
title: Generate Titles
description:
Generate scored YouTube title suggestions.

Once a result is ready, offer vidiq_youtube_preview to show the thumbnail and title beside real YouTube competitors.

Provide at least one of `videoId`, `title`, or `description`. With
only `videoId`, the current title/description are fetched from YouTube.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or video URL. When provided, the tool fetches the current title/description from yt-proxy to ground generation. Optional when title and/or description are supplied directly.

title.description: Current/working video title. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value takes precedence.

description.description: Current video description. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value takes precedence.

numTitles.description: How many title candidates to generate (default: 3)

type.description: Video format hint. Affects the generation prompt and scoring rubric. When omitted, upstream infers from duration and otherwise treats the video as long-form.

language.description: Target language for generated titles and the analysis pass (e.g. 'en', 'pt-BR'). Defaults to English when omitted.

regionCode.description: 2-letter ISO country code (e.g. 'US', 'BR'). Normalized to uppercase. Used by upstream when fetching competitive context.

scoreThreshold.description: Return only suggestions with score >= threshold. Thresholds above 70 on long-form videos may legitimately yield no results, and the filter applies before the numTitles top-K slice (so the response may contain fewer items than numTitles).

previousTitles.description: Recent titles from the same channel. Used by upstream to reduce repetition and improve novelty. Capped at 20 entries x 200 chars; duplicates removed.

competitorTitles.description: Seed titles for the competitive context block. When provided, upstream skips its Outliers lookup and uses these directly — useful for deterministic output or when the caller already has a curated competitor set. Capped at 20 entries x 200 chars; duplicates removed.

analysisSummary.description: Pre-computed analysis summary. When provided, upstream skips its own analysis pass (transcript/frames → Gemini) and uses this directly. Useful when chaining after a tool that already produced video understanding. Capped at 4000 chars.

nextStep.description: What to offer the user next.

name: vidiq_generate_comment_replies
title: Generate YouTube Comment Replies
description:
Generate multiple draft replies to one viewer comment on a YouTube video, with one reply per requested tone. Use this when the user wants response ideas for a specific comment. To retrieve comments first, use `vidiq_video_comments`.

Provide the video's title and the exact viewer comment. Optionally provide 3–10 tone labels; otherwise the defaults are General, Humorous, Thankful, Witty, and Informal.

This tool returns draft text only. It never posts or otherwise changes anything on YouTube.

Cost: 1 credit(s) per call.

title.description: Title of the YouTube video that received the viewer comment.

comment.description: Viewer comment to draft replies for.

tones.description: Three to ten tone labels for the reply options. Defaults to General, Humorous, Thankful, Witty, and Informal.

items.description: Tone label to use for one reply option.

title.description: Video title used to generate the replies.

tone.description: Tone used for this generated reply.

reply.description: Generated reply text. Review it before posting to YouTube.

replies.description: Generated reply options, one per requested tone.

name: vidiq_generate_thumbnail
title: Generate Thumbnail or Image
description:
Generate a YouTube thumbnail.

Once a result is ready, offer vidiq_youtube_preview to show the thumbnail and title beside real YouTube competitors.

Provide at least one of videoId, title, description, or userQuery. With only a videoId, the video's current
title, description, and thumbnail are pulled in automatically.

For an image that is not a thumbnail, use `vidiq_image_generate`.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until
it is "completed" to get the thumbnail (shown inline) with its imageUrl, a self-score, and short feedback.
A request sent without purpose that clearly asks for another kind of image may come back as an image: its result
is marked purpose "image" and has no score or feedback.
Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if generation fails.

Include the imageUrl in your reply so the user can open or save the file. The inline preview isn't downloadable.

Treat the score as a rough estimate rather than a verdict: don't lead with it, and don't regenerate just to
raise it. To iterate, change one thing at a time and keep the best result. For a reliable critique, use
vidiq_score_thumbnail.

Cost: 22 credit(s) per thumbnail; a picture with purpose "image" costs at most 22, and the result says what was charged.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or video URL. When provided, title, description, and currentThumbnail are auto-filled from YouTube unless the caller supplies them explicitly. Optional when at least one of title, description, or userQuery is given.

title.description: Video title used for grounding. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value wins.

description.description: Video description used for grounding. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value wins.

transcript.description: Optional transcript text. Used for subject detection in Quick Generate and as context in Pro Generate. Pair with vidiq_video_transcript when available.

userQuery.description: Natural-language creative direction (e.g. 'show the host pointing at a glowing dollar sign'). Highest-priority generation signal upstream.

purpose.description: Legacy: use vidiq_image_generate for images that are not thumbnails. Still accepted. What the result is for. 'thumbnail' designs a YouTube thumbnail and returns a score with feedback. 'image' is for anything else the user wants drawn for their video, such as a story frame, scene illustration, character art or background: userQuery is rendered as written, with any images sent as its references and the title as context only. Description, transcript, feedback and the video behind videoId are not used, and no score or feedback is returned. 'image' requires userQuery. Omit it only for a thumbnail. A request sent without it that clearly asks for another kind of image may be rendered as an image; send 'thumbnail' to always get a thumbnail.

currentThumbnail.description: An existing/current thumbnail to reference for composition, a hosted image URL or an uploaded image. When omitted but videoId is provided, auto-filled with the best available resolution of the video's YouTube thumbnail.

subjectImage.description: A subject/person image, a hosted image URL or an uploaded image. Highest-priority likeness reference for the main face in the thumbnail.

referenceImages.description: Reference thumbnails to emulate style/composition, hosted image URLs or uploaded images. Presence of this field switches the request out of Quick Generate into the Pro / Improve flow upstream. With purpose 'image' they are instead the images userQuery refers to. Capped at 10 entries; duplicates removed.

currentThumbnailId.description: currentThumbnail as the imageId of a picture in the user's vidIQ image library, as the upload picker or vidiq_upload_image returns it. Send it instead of currentThumbnail.

subjectImageId.description: subjectImage as the imageId of a picture in the user's vidIQ image library, as the upload picker or vidiq_upload_image returns it. Send it instead of subjectImage.

referenceImageIds.description: referenceImages as library imageIds, read like them and counted with them: 10 in all.

orientation.description: Orientation. 'landscape' is the standard 16:9 YouTube thumbnail (default when omitted); 'portrait' is a 9:16 Shorts thumbnail. 'square' is 1:1, for an avatar or logo, and needs purpose 'image'.

background.description: Send 'transparent' for one subject on a transparent background, delivered as a PNG to layer over a video or design: a character, object, logo or sticker. Describe only the subject in userQuery. Needs purpose 'image'. Omit it for a scene or any image with its own background.

score.description: Overall quality score (0–100) returned by the previous scoring call.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of this finding.

pointImpact.description: Point delta this finding contributed to the overall score (when available).

strengths.description: Findings to preserve in the next iteration.

name: vidiq_media_upscale
title: Upscale an image or video
description:
Makes a picture 4K: the same image with its long edge at 3840 px and its shape kept (3840x2160 for a thumbnail), sharper and with finer detail. It answers at once with a JPEG link and when it stops working. Send a picture made with vidIQ by its imageUrl in image, or the user's own, attached or uploaded, in imageFile. A picture already 3840 px or larger is refused. Makes a video made with vidiq_generate_video 2K or 4K: send its finished job's mcpJobId and target. It starts a job: poll it with vidiq_job_poll for the larger video's URL. A video of up to 24 s can be made 2K, of up to 11 s 4K; a video already at the size asked for (one made at 2K, made 2K) is refused, so don't offer that size. Use it when the user asks for 4K, 2K, a higher resolution, an upscale, or a sharper or crisper version of a thumbnail or image or video. When the user has a finished thumbnail or image or video, you may offer it once, with its price. Call it only when the user asked for it or said yes: never on your own, as it charges credits. Not for changing what it shows, its text, its crop or its length.

Cost: 5 credits for each new picture 4K, and nothing for the same picture again; a video costs 5 credits per second at 2K and 10 at 4K.

image.description: A picture as an image link, such as the imageUrl another vidIQ tool returned, or as a base64 data URI. Use imageFile instead for a picture the user attached or uploaded. Exactly one of image, imageFile, mcpJobId is required.

imageFile.description: A picture from the user's vidIQ image library, as the imageId from vidiq_file_upload. For an image attached in chat or on the user's device, open vidiq_file_upload so the user can upload it. Exactly one of image, imageFile, mcpJobId is required.

renewOnly.description: Only sign the 4K already made of this picture anew: never make, or charge for, a new one.

mcpJobId.description: A video: the mcpJobId of a finished vidiq_generate_video job on this account. Exactly one of image, imageFile, mcpJobId is required.

target.description: With mcpJobId: how large to make the video, 2k or 4k. A picture is made 4K.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

name: vidiq_image_generate
title: Generate Images
description:
Generate an image on Nano Banana Pro, Nano Banana 2.1, GPT Image 2.6 or Ideogram 4.6 from a text prompt, or a set of images from several, optionally guided by reference images.

Use this when the user asks for an image, picture, illustration, character, logo, sticker or background, for the frames of a story or for the scenes of a video. Send `model` only when the user's own message names a model, never by your own choice, and never switch models silently; a finished image names the model that drew it. Never use it for a YouTube thumbnail: `vidiq_generate_thumbnail` designs those.

Ask for several images in ONE call, an entry of `images` each, not one call per image: they are made at once and shown together. To keep a character or product the same across images, pass a picture of it in referenceImages (referenceImageFiles for a ChatGPT upload); if the user has none, make that picture first and pass its imageUrl in referenceImages.

Runs asynchronously: returns an mcpJobId for each image. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with each id until it is "completed" to get its imageUrl, and include the links in your reply so the user can open or save the files.

Cost per image: at most 22 credit(s) with no model named, at most 28 with one; the result says what was charged. Charged as each starts; an image that fails is refunded automatically. Before starting a set, tell the user the most it can cost.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

prompt.description: What this image shows (1–2000 chars). It is rendered as written. Name a recurring character or product the same way in every prompt.

images.description: One entry per image (1–8): one entry for a single image, several for a set such as the scenes of a video or the frames of a story. They are made at once and shown together in one card.

aspectRatio.description: Optional. The shape of every image: 16:9 landscape (the default), 9:16 portrait, or 1:1 square for an avatar or logo.

referenceImages.description: Optional. Pictures used for every image: a character, product or style to keep, or a picture to change. Hosted image URLs, such as the imageUrl of an earlier result, base64 data URIs, or the imageId of a picture the user uploaded to their vidIQ image library with the upload picker. Capped at 10 entries together with referenceImageFiles; duplicates removed.

referenceImageFiles.description: Optional. The same, for pictures the user uploaded in ChatGPT. The imageUrl of an earlier result goes in referenceImages, not here.

background.description: Optional. Send 'transparent' for one subject on a transparent background, delivered as a PNG to layer over a video or design: a character, object, logo or sticker. Describe only the subject in each prompt. Omit it for a scene or any image with its own background.

model.description: Optional. Leave it out unless the user's own message names an image model; then send that one. Never pick a model yourself, not for photos, likeness, text, quality or any other reason: left out, one is chosen for each image. Only when the user asks which model to use, answer from this: nano_banana_pro = Nano Banana Pro, likeness, edits from reference images, complex scenes; nano_banana_2_1 = Nano Banana 2.1, fast all-rounder; gpt_image_2_6 = GPT Image 2.6, accurate text and layouts; ideogram_4_6 = Ideogram 4.6, typography, posters and logos. A transparent background is only drawn on gpt_image_2_6.

name: vidiq_refine_thumbnail
title: Refine Thumbnail
description:
Change or improve a YouTube thumbnail by describing what you want in plain words.

Give it the thumbnail to change as sourceThumbnail (a hosted URL) or sourceThumbnailFile (a ChatGPT upload),
and say what to change (instructions) — for example "make the text bigger" or "change the background to a
football stadium".

This edits thumbnails. To change an image made with vidiq_generate_thumbnail purpose "image", call that tool
again with purpose "image", the image in referenceImages and the change in userQuery.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until
it is "completed" to get the updated thumbnail (shown inline) with its imageUrl, a self-score, and short
feedback; an edit made with a mask has no score. Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if
refinement fails.

Include the imageUrl in your reply so the user can open or save the file. The inline preview isn't downloadable.

Cost: 22 credit(s) per call.

sourceThumbnail.description: The thumbnail you want to change as a hosted image URL, a base64 data URI, or the imageId of a picture in the user's vidIQ image library, as the upload picker or vidiq_upload_image returns it. Usually this is the imageUrl from vidiq_generate_thumbnail. Use sourceThumbnailFile instead for a ChatGPT file upload.

sourceThumbnailFile.description: The thumbnail you want to change as a ChatGPT-uploaded file. Use this instead of sourceThumbnail when the user uploads the source image.

instructions.description: What you want changed, in plain words, for example 'make the background darker' or 'make the face bigger'. Describe the change, not the whole picture.

originalConcept.description: Optional. A short description of what the original thumbnail shows. Helps keep the result on-topic. If left out, your instructions are used.

videoId.description: Optional. The YouTube video this thumbnail is for, as an 11-character video ID or a YouTube video URL.

title.description: Optional. The video's title. The result is scored against it, so send the title the thumbnail was made or scored with to keep the scores comparable.

subjectImage.description: Optional. A photo of the person who should be the main face in the thumbnail as a hosted image URL, a base64 data URI, or the imageId of a picture in the user's vidIQ image library, as the upload picker or vidiq_upload_image returns it.

referenceImages.description: Optional. Up to 10 thumbnails whose style you'd like to copy, each a hosted image URL, a base64 data URI or a library imageId.

mask.description: Optional. To change only one area and leave the rest untouched, provide a base64 PNG, JPEG, or WebP image (raw base64 or a data:image/...;base64 URI) that marks the area to change.

points.description: Optional. Changes pinned to places on the thumbnail, each with its own instruction, for example 'remove this' on a logo. Cannot be combined with mask.

x.description: Fraction of the width from the left edge, 0 to 1.

y.description: Fraction of the height from the top edge, 0 to 1.

instruction.description: What to change at this place.

markup.description: Optional. A copy of the thumbnail with marks drawn on it (circles, arrows, outlines) showing where the instructions apply, as a hosted image URL, a base64 data URI or a library imageId. The marks are left out of the result. Cannot be combined with mask.

orientation.description: Thumbnail orientation. 'landscape' is the standard 16:9 YouTube thumbnail (default when omitted); 'portrait' is a 9:16 Shorts thumbnail. Ignored when a mask is supplied (mask edits keep the source dimensions).

name: vidiq_video_watch
title: Watch Video
description:
Watch a long-form YouTube video end-to-end and return a structured markdown walkthrough.

Use this tool to:
- Understand what happens visually in a video (not just what is said) — useful when transcripts miss context
- Generate scene-by-scene breakdowns with timestamps for editing or analysis
- Answer specific questions about a video by passing a custom `prompt`
- Compare visual structure across videos for SEO / hook research

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it is "completed" to get the markdown walkthrough in the `analysisText` field. Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if the analysis fails.

Videos up to 6 hours long are supported; longer ones are refused before any credits are charged. For short-form content, use `vidiq_watch_shortform_content` instead.

Note: prefer `vidiq_video_transcript` when you only need spoken words, since it is faster and cheaper.

Your own video file: pass `videoUrl` instead of `video` (your vidIQ upload, generated or composed video, a `vidiq_generate_clips` clipUrl, or a `vidiq_edit_media` mediaUrl) to check a clip, and ask the question in `prompt`, e.g. whether a prop stays attached through an action. A file costs 5 credits when it is at most 60 s and 50 MB, 10 credits when it is at most 180 s and 150 MB, otherwise 25 credits; refunded if the analysis fails. Before watching several files, tell the user the total (`vidiq_media_file_info` gives each file's length and size at no charge). MP4/MOV up to 1 GiB and 10 minutes; a file that is not yours is refused before any charge. Some accounts can only watch YouTube videos for now: a file refused with `file_source_unavailable` costs nothing; watch a YouTube video with `video` instead.

Cost: 25 credit(s) per YouTube video; a video file as priced above.

video.description: Long-form YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or watch/youtu.be URL. For short-form content, use vidiq_watch_shortform_content instead.

prompt.description: Optional custom analysis instruction. If omitted, a scene-by-scene markdown walkthrough is produced (timestamped ### Scene N: Label headers + ### Summary bullets). Markdown structure is enforced regardless — do not ask for JSON.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

Supply exactly one of video or videoUrl. A file costs 5 credits when it is at most 60 s and 50 MB, 10 credits when it is at most 180 s and 150 MB, otherwise 25 credits; before watching several files, tell the user the total. Files: MP4/MOV, at most 1 GiB and 10 minutes. Some accounts can only watch YouTube videos for now: on file_source_unavailable, use video instead.

name: vidiq_watch_shortform_content
title: Watch Short-Form Content
description:
Watch one piece of short-form content from Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube and return a markdown scene-by-scene walkthrough.

Pass the full public URL. For YouTube Shorts, a /shorts/, watch, or youtu.be URL is accepted; the content is verified to be short-form. Call this tool in parallel to compare multiple pieces of short-form content.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it is "completed" to get the walkthrough. Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if the analysis fails.

A photo or carousel post (an Instagram /p/ photo post, a TikTok photo post) has nothing to watch: it costs 1 credit and returns its slides as images at once, with no job to poll.

To import an Instagram or TikTok video as reusable footage, use vidiq_video_upload (not available on every account yet).

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Long-form YouTube videos — use `vidiq_video_watch`.
- Bare platform IDs or Instagram shortcodes — pass a full URL.

Cost: 10 credit(s) per call.

url.description: Full URL to short-form content on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. TikTok share links (vm.tiktok.com, tiktok.com/t/...) are accepted; bare platform IDs are not.

prompt.description: Optional custom analysis instruction. Omit it for the tuned scene-by-scene walkthrough. Markdown output only; do not ask for JSON.

name: vidiq_ig_profile
title: Instagram Profile
description:
Public data only. For the user's own performance, check `vidiq_social_account_list` first for private insights. Fetch public Instagram profile by handle: bio, follower/following counts, post count, verification, external URL, with the profile picture returned inline.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Profile search/discovery — you must already have a handle.
- Reels — use `vidiq_ig_profile_reels` (up to 12 Reels per call, pinned Reels first and others newest-first. Pass nextUntil as until for older Reels. Each call is charged).
- Stories, Highlights, IGTV, private-account data.
- Engagement-rate or growth analytics — snapshot only.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

name: vidiq_ig_profile_reels
title: Instagram Profile Reels
description:
Public data only. For the user's own performance, check `vidiq_social_account_list` first for private insights. Fetch a creator's reels by handle: shortcode, caption, play/like/comment counts, duration, timestamp, pinned-profile status, with every reel's cover in one contact-sheet image, 3 per row. Form a full Instagram reel URL from a returned shortcode before passing that short-form content URL to `vidiq_watch_shortform_content`.

Returns up to 12 reels per call. Pinned reels appear first on the latest page, followed by unpinned reels newest-first. For older reels, pass the returned nextUntil as until. Each call is charged.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Strict newest-first ordering across the whole response — older pinned reels may appear before newer unpinned reels.
- Image posts, carousels, Stories.
- Account, creator, influencer, or competitor-account discovery - use `vidiq_instagram_account_discovery`.
- Cross-platform outlier examples or topic search - use `vidiq_instagram_tiktok_outlier_search` (cannot filter by handle).

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

handle.description: Instagram handle (with or without leading @) or profile URL such as https://www.instagram.com/<handle>/. Handle: 1-30 chars; letters/digits/dot/underscore.

name: vidiq_instagram_comment_list
title: List Instagram Comments
description:
Read what people say under a public Instagram post or reel: one page of top-level comments (about 15), pinned and most relevant first, with likes, reply counts, dates, and whether the creator pinned or liked each. Commenter usernames are not included. Use this when the user wants audience reaction, viewer questions or objections, or buying intent on a specific post.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Comment counts — `vidiq_ig_profile_reels` already has them.
- Replies to a comment — top-level comments only.
- TikTok comments — `vidiq_tiktok_comment_list`. YouTube comments — `vidiq_video_comments`.

Public data only. Fetch a public TikTok profile by handle: nickname, bio, bio link, verification, follower/following counts, total likes and video count, with the profile picture returned inline as an image.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Finding creators in a niche — use `vidiq_tiktok_account_discovery`. For breakout TikToks across a niche, use `vidiq_instagram_tiktok_outlier_search`.

handle.description: TikTok handle (with or without leading @) or profile URL such as https://www.tiktok.com/@<handle>.

name: vidiq_tiktok_profile_videos
title: TikTok Profile Videos
description:
Public data only. Fetch a TikTok creator's latest videos by handle, about 10 per call, newest first: video URL, caption, view/like/comment/share/save counts, duration, post date, pinned/promoted/paid-partnership flags, with every video's cover in one contact-sheet image, 3 per row. "Promoted" means the creator paid to run the post as a TikTok ad. Collabs posted by another creator are labelled with that creator's handle.

For older videos, pass the returned nextUntil as until; each call is charged.

Pass a returned video URL to `vidiq_watch_shortform_content` to analyze it, or to `vidiq_tiktok_comment_list` for its comments.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Account details (bio, followers) — use `vidiq_tiktok_profile`.
- Breakout TikToks across a niche or topic — use `vidiq_instagram_tiktok_outlier_search` (cannot filter by handle).
- Instagram creators — use `vidiq_ig_profile_reels`.

name: vidiq_list_competitors

List the YouTube channels the user is tracking as competitors of one of their own channels.

youtubeChannelId.description: YouTube channel ID (e.g. 'UCxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx') of one of the user's own authorized channels. Use vidiq_user_channels first if you don't know which channels the user owns.

name: vidiq_bookmarks_list
title: List Bookmarks
description:
Retrieve the signed-in user's saved bookmarks to review or reuse in research and planning. Use when the user asks "show my saved videos", "show my saved channels", "show my saved keywords", "show my generated videos", "show my uploads", "what did I bookmark?", or wants to reuse saved inspiration or a saved creation. With no arguments, returns the 10 newest bookmarks across all types. Video bookmarks span several types: bookmarkType="saved-video" (videos saved while browsing, any platform), "saved-outlier-video" (YouTube outliers), "saved-generated-video" (the user's own generated videos) and "saved-uploaded-video" (their uploads); channels and creators use "saved-channel" (platform youtube, instagram or tiktok); keywords use "saved-keyword". When the user asks for "saved videos" without saying which, ask whether they mean all of them, outliers only, generated, or uploads — or list all types and group the answer by type. Tags match any supplied tag name. Supports type and tag filters, not keyword or topic search. Returns stored payloads, not live metrics; use the relevant research tool when fresh metrics are requested. Pass nextOffset as offset for the next page; null means no more results.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

bookmarkType.description: Filter by type, e.g. saved-video, saved-channel, saved-outlier-video, saved-generated-video, saved-uploaded-video or saved-keyword; omit for all types.

tags.description: Match any of these tag names.

name: vidiq_bookmarks_save
title: Save Bookmarks
description:
Save 1–50 bookmarks of one type to the signed-in account in one atomic batch. Only save items the user explicitly asked to save. Repeated saves create duplicates. Do not automatically retry a failed save; inspect saved bookmarks first if the outcome is uncertain. After success, briefly confirm the saved count and what was saved. The response includes a suggested vidiq_bookmarks_list call for later retrieval; do not call it automatically just to confirm a successful save.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

bookmarkType.description: Configured type shared by every payload, e.g. saved-video, saved-channel, saved-keyword, saved-outlier-video, saved-generated-video or saved-uploaded-video.

tags.description: Existing tag IDs applied to every item.

payloads.description:
1–50 payloads of the selected bookmarkType. Common field mappings, subject to the configured type schema:
- saved-video: videoId (YouTube ID, Instagram shortcode, or TikTok video ID), title, platform (youtube, instagram, or tiktok), type (long or short).
- saved-channel (a creator profile on any supported platform): platform (youtube, instagram, or tiktok), channelId (a YouTube channel ID when platform=youtube; a profile handle when platform=instagram or tiktok), title (display name).
- saved-outlier-video: videoId from the selected YouTube outlier.
- saved-keyword: keyword (question in questions mode); when available, competition, overall→overallScore, estimatedMonthlySearch→searchVolume. Omit unavailable metrics; preserve zero. Never use volume or countryVolume as searchVolume; zero estimatedMonthlySearch means below the reporting threshold.
- saved-generated-video: projectId, videoUrl, prompt, model, resolution, duration→durationSeconds from the completed generation result.
- saved-uploaded-video: uploadId, title (the title provided when uploading), duration→durationSeconds. Omit videoUrl because it expires.
Use values from tool inputs and results; do not invent missing fields.

ids.description: Saved bookmark IDs in payload order.

retrieveWith.description: Suggested call to browse bookmarks of this type, including previously saved items.

name: vidiq_bookmarks_remove
title: Remove Bookmarks
description:
Remove 1–50 bookmarks from the signed-in account in one atomic batch. Only remove items the user explicitly asked to remove; otherwise ask first. Duplicate IDs count once. Any unknown, already removed, or foreign ID rejects the entire batch. If the outcome is uncertain, inspect saved bookmarks before retrying.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

name: vidiq_update_competitors
title: Update Competitors
description:
Follow or unfollow competitor channels for one of the user's own YouTube channels.

- youtubeChannelId must be a channel the user has authorized (call vidiq_user_channels to discover).
- follow / unfollow are arrays of YouTube channel IDs — they must not overlap; at least one must be non-empty.
- Plan-based caps apply. Adding above the cap fails. Returns the resulting tracked-competitors list (channel IDs only).

Example arguments: { "youtubeChannelId": "UC_x5XG1OV2P6uZZ5FSM9Ttw", "follow": ["UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA"], "unfollow": [] }

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

youtubeChannelId.description: YouTube channel ID (starts with 'UC', e.g. 'UC_x5XG1OV2P6uZZ5FSM9Ttw') of one of the user's own authorized channels. Call vidiq_user_channels first if unknown.

follow.description: Array of up to 50 YouTube channel IDs to start tracking as competitors, e.g. ["UC_x5XG1OV2P6uZZ5FSM9Ttw","UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA"].

unfollow.description: Array of up to 50 YouTube channel IDs to stop tracking, e.g. ["UC_x5XG1OV2P6uZZ5FSM9Ttw"].

name: vidiq_youtube_ab_test_list
title: List A/B Tests
description:
List the user's saved YouTube title and thumbnail A/B tests with filters, counts, watch-time shares and pagination. Results need the vidIQ browser extension; each page that returns tests is a separate paid call, and an empty page is free. Use vidiq_youtube_ab_test_insights_generate for patterns and a suggested next test. Use vidiq_channel_analytics_extended report=ab_tests only when the user explicitly asks for a live read from YouTube Studio. Cannot start, stop or edit a YouTube test.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

channelId.description: Owned YouTube channel. Omit for the user's only connected owner channel.

thumbnailUrl.description: This variant's thumbnail. Hosts cannot open the link; to see the picture, pass it to vidiq_get_images as kind thumbnail_snapshot.

watchTimeShare.description: Watch-time share, not CTR; YouTube uses it to choose winners.

edgePoints.description: (watchTimeShare - 1/variantCount) * 100. Use this to compare two- and three-variant tests, not raw shares.

isLeader.description: Current snapshot leader; distinct from winner and applied variant.

channelTotal.description: All saved tests on the channel, independent of filters and pagination.

observedAt.description: When vidIQ last saved any of this channel's tests from YouTube Studio.

oldestRunningObservedAt.description: Oldest save time among running tests; their shares are snapshots from then.

stale.description: True when the tests were last saved more than 24 hours ago; false when none are saved. Finished tests are unaffected; only running tests and tests started after observedAt can differ from YouTube Studio.

videosWithoutSavedTests.description: No saved row for these requested videos; this does not prove they never ran a test.

name: vidiq_youtube_ab_test_insights_generate
title: Generate A/B Test Insights
description:
Find patterns and noise in the user's saved YouTube title and thumbnail A/B tests and suggest a next title test. Current stored insights and insufficient-history results are free, even at zero balance. Otherwise starts a paid analysis; collect it with vidiq_job_poll using mcpJobId. Failed analysis or insufficient evidence is refunded. Only one analysis per user can be in progress. Use vidiq_youtube_ab_test_list for saved test rows and filters, and vidiq_channel_analytics_extended report=ab_tests only when the user explicitly asks for a live read from YouTube Studio. Does not start a test on YouTube.

Cost: 100 credit(s) per call.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

channelId.description: Owned YouTube channel. Omit for the user's only connected owner channel.

refresh.description: Force a new paid analysis instead of a current ready result. Cannot override insufficient_evidence for unchanged evidence.

coverage.description: Finished saved tests, and per category how many are finished and how many this analysis read. Every usable title test is read; thumbnail analysis reads at most 48 images, and only tests with usable images, so analyzed can be far below finished. State the analyzed count when describing a pattern. Absent when unknown.

status.description: inprogress: a paid analysis started; poll vidiq_job_poll with mcpJobId.

mcpJobId.description: Set only when status is inprogress.

testedAt.description: Test start time; identify a saved test by videoId plus testedAt.

edgePoints.description: Watch-time share above an even split, in percentage points; not CTR. Treat patterns as observations rather than proof.

testedAt.description: Test start time; identify a saved test by videoId plus testedAt.

edgePoints.description: Watch-time share above an even split, in percentage points; not CTR. Treat patterns as observations rather than proof.

name: vidiq_channel_analytics_extended
title: Channel Analytics Extended
description:
Get thumbnail impressions and CTR, views and watch time by UTC hour, viewer online times, Studio Trends and content gaps, Shorts stayed-to-watch versus swiped-away, copyright claims, age restrictions, monetization status, end-screen configuration and clicks, and existing YouTube title or thumbnail test results for the user's own channel. See report and analyticsReport for options, including unique reach breakdowns. Also YouTube's live search suggestions (autocomplete) for any phrase, with report search_suggestions.

Starts an on-demand report request through the user's connected vidIQ browser extension. The browser must be running and signed in to Google with access to the requested channel. Reads do not change videos, channel settings or A/B tests.

Use supplied video IDs. Ask for required videos or dates that are missing. Date ranges use YouTube reporting days with an exclusive endDate. Hourly reports require whole UTC hours and an exclusive endTime. Do not round partial hours or substitute another report; ask for a supported window.

Report numbers as returned: preserve zeros, treat null as unavailable, and never reconstruct CTR or stayed-to-watch from other fields. retrievedAt is retrieval time, not data freshness.

Use vidiq_channel_analytics for whole-day views, watch time, engaged views, demographics, geography, traffic sources, devices and search terms. Use vidiq_keyword_research for general keyword demand.

On extension_not_connected, call vidiq_connect_extension with the same report to show connection steps, then wait for the user to retry. If that tool is unavailable, relay the returned message. On processing, call again with only the returned jobId to retrieve the same report.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID (UC…) to read. Omit to use the user's only connected channel, or infer it when every requested videoIds entry is found and belongs to the same connected channel with owner access.

jobId.description: ID returned for a report that is still processing. Pass only jobId to retrieve that report.

userGoal.description: Optional. The user's underlying goal behind this request, in one short sentence in your own words (e.g. 'find video ideas to grow a new cooking channel past 1k subscribers'). Up to 300 characters. Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or conversation history.

report.description:
What to read; required unless resuming with jobId.
thumbnail_ctr: thumbnail impressions and CTR per video over a date range. thumbnail_ctr requires 1–50 videoIds, startDate and an exclusive endDate. There is no whole-channel thumbnail CTR mode without video IDs. Ask for the missing videos and dates before calling the report; never invent them.
video_performance: views and watch time per video over whole UTC hours, up to 7 days. Needs 1–50 videoIds, startTime and endTime; no dates or engaged views.
audience: when viewers are online (UTC relative activity, 28 days), new, casual and regular viewer shares, other channels they watch (28 days) and other content they watch (7 days). No custom dates. Suppressed data means too little data, not zero viewers.
trends: the channel's personalized Studio Trends feed, or one topic's details and content gaps with topic. No custom dates. Generic empty-state suggestions are not measured demand.
shorts_watch: channel-wide Shorts stayed-to-watch versus swiped-away for Studio's last 28 days. No video filter or dates. Not thumbnail CTR or a retention curve.
shorts_stayed_to_watch: per-Short stayed-to-watch, Shorts feed impressions and views over startDate and exclusive endDate; no videoIds. Use it to rank Shorts or compare 28-day periods, one request per period, following nextPageOffset to the last page (50 rows a page, at most 500 Shorts, sorted by feed impressions); at the cap, say coverage is incomplete. Views include all traffic and are not the stayed-to-watch numerator. It measures the choice to keep watching, not completion; compare feed sample sizes and look at the actual openings before judging hooks.
restrictions: copyright claims, age restriction and monetization status per video.
end_screens: configured end-screen elements, timing and destinations; for clicks use advanced_analytics with end_screen_elements or end_screen_types.
advanced_analytics: additional per-video metrics and breakdowns selected by analyticsReport, for exactly one video over startDate and exclusive endDate. Use vidiq_channel_analytics for ordinary views or watch time, search terms, external referrers, countries or cities, device or operating-system performance, sharing services, ad types, Premium, playlists and aggregate card metrics. If that tool lacks a metric, explain the limitation. Supports per-card and unique-reach breakdowns. No custom metrics, memberships, posts or live engagement.
ab_tests: existing YouTube title and thumbnail tests (Test & Compare): status, result and each variant's watch-time share. YouTube picks winners by watch-time share; preserve inconclusive and notEnoughData outcomes. Results may be saved rather than freshly read; check source and stale before describing freshness.
search_suggestions: YouTube's live search suggestions (autocomplete) for query: what people type into YouTube search right now, in YouTube's own order, for any country and language. Public data, not the user's channel: it needs no channel, channelId or Google sign-in, only the extension. Suggestions carry no search volume; measure a phrase with vidiq_keyword_research. Start with expand none; use questions for question searches, and letters or all only when the user wants a long list. When result.partial is true, say the list is incomplete.

analyticsReport.description:
When report is "advanced_analytics", choose one analytics breakdown below. Required for that report; omit for other reports or when resuming with jobId.
end_screen_elements: Clicks, impressions and CTR for each end-screen element, plus its current destination configuration.
end_screen_types: End-screen clicks, impressions and CTR by element type.
thumbnail_traffic_sources: Thumbnail impressions and CTR by traffic source.
thumbnail_suggested_videos: Thumbnail impressions and CTR by referring suggested-video ID.
new_returning_viewers: Thumbnail and viewing performance for new versus returning viewers.
audience_watch_behavior: Thumbnail and viewing performance for new, casual and regular viewers.
audience_counts: Estimated unique, new, returning, casual and regular viewers, plus views per viewer.
unique_reach_devices: Unique reach by device.
unique_reach_operating_systems: Unique reach by operating system.
age_watch_time: Average viewing duration by age group.
gender_watch_time: Average viewing duration by gender.
subscription_sources: Subscriber gains and losses by subscription source.
caption_languages: Viewing performance by caption or subtitle language.
metadata_languages: Viewing performance by translated title and description language.
audio_languages: Viewing performance by audio-track language.
translation_use: Viewing performance for original versus translated content.
player_types: Viewing performance by embedded player mode.
transactions: Transaction revenue and counts by business model.
card_elements: Card and teaser performance by card ID.
card_types: Card and teaser performance by card type.
shopping_products: Shopping clicks and impressions by product.
shopping_sellers: Shopping orders, sales and commissions by seller.
remixes: Remix count and remix views.
remix_sources: Remix views by derived video ID.
clips: Community clip views and watch time.
hype: Hypes and hype points.

pageOffset.description: advanced_analytics and shorts_stayed_to_watch: zero-based page offset. Omit for the first 50 rows; continue only with nextPageOffset from the previous result. Totals reports have no pagination.

topic.description: trends only: a topic to explore. Omit for the channel's personalized Studio Trends feed.

videoIds.description: Required for thumbnail_ctr, video_performance, restrictions and end_screens: 1–50 YouTube video IDs (1–10 for end_screens). advanced_analytics requires exactly one video ID. Optional only for ab_tests (omit for the channel's latest tests). Do not pass videoIds for audience, trends, shorts_watch or shorts_stayed_to_watch.

startDate.description: thumbnail_ctr, advanced_analytics and shorts_stayed_to_watch: first day (YYYY-MM-DD) in YouTube reporting time.

endDate.description: thumbnail_ctr, advanced_analytics and shorts_stayed_to_watch: exclusive end day (YYYY-MM-DD), after startDate.

startTime.description: video_performance only: required window start as a whole UTC hour (e.g. 2026-10-20T14:00:00Z).

endTime.description: video_performance only: required exclusive window end as a whole UTC hour (e.g. 2026-10-20T18:00:00Z), at most 7 days after startTime.

query.description: search_suggestions only, required: what someone would type into YouTube search, e.g. 'home workout'. Up to 100 characters.

country.description: search_suggestions only: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country to get suggestions for, e.g. 'US'. Omit for the country the user's browser is in.

language.description: search_suggestions only: language of the suggestions, e.g. 'en' or 'pt-BR'. Omit unless the user asks for one or writes in one: omitted, it is the connected channel's language, else en.

expand.description: search_suggestions only: how far to widen the query. none (default): YouTube's 10–15 suggestions for the query itself. letters: also the query followed by each of a–z and 0–9, a few hundred phrases. questions: only question searches around the query (en, es, pt, ru, de, fr, hi, ja). all: every expansion, including prepositions; the longest list and the slowest call.

limit.description: search_suggestions only: max suggestions to return (default 100, max 1000). The query's own suggestions always come first; a shorter list then keeps the top-ranked suggestions of every expansion.

result.description: The requested YouTube report. retrievedAt is the retrieval time, not a guarantee of data freshness. Unavailable values are null; zeros are real. Report CTR and stayed-to-watch as returned, without reconstructing them from other fields. audience: viewersOnline (relative activity, 168 UTC slots starting Sunday; not viewer counts), viewerSegments (new/casual/regular ratios, 0–1), otherChannels (28 days) and otherContent (7 days). trends: availability, contentGapsAvailability and shelves with queries/videos; empty_state is generic inspiration, not personalized demand. shorts_stayed_to_watch: startDate, exclusive endDate, rows with videoId, stayedToWatchPercentage (0–100), shortsFeedImpressions and views. Studio totals are separate from rows; columns and anomalies describe missing/processing data. Follow nextPageOffset for 50-row pages, up to 500 Shorts. truncated=true with no nextPageOffset means coverage is capped. shorts_watch: periodDays=28, availability, stayedToWatchPercentage and swipedAwayPercentage (0–100). Suppressed or unavailable Studio cards are not evidence of zero viewers or zero demand. thumbnail_ctr: startDate, exclusive endDate and per-video availability (available, partial, unavailable or not_returned), thumbnailImpressions and thumbnailCtrPercentage (0–100). video_performance: the UTC hour window (startTime/endTime) and per video views and watchTimeMinutes; no engaged views. restrictions: per video title, claimDetails, statusDetails, monetizedStatus, ageRestriction and selfCertification as Studio reports them. claimDetails.videoHasCommercialBlock alone does not establish blocked visibility or reduced reach; a copyright claim can have no impact on reach. end_screens: configured elements, destinations and timing per video; [] means no configured end screen. advanced_analytics: the selected report's breakdown, rows, column units and totals. Counts remain counts, duration is milliseconds, percentages use 0–100 units (reported outliers are preserved), ratios are unscaled, currency values are USD units. availability=empty means no rows returned, not zero activity. partial/unavailable describe missing cells; anomalies and totalsAnomalies describe processing or missing coverage even when availability=available. Use nextPageOffset for another page; truncated=true means more rows may exist, including at the 500-row cap. Never sum audience rows or average CTRs to manufacture totals. End-screen rows preserve currentConfiguration; currentDestinationVideoId is set only for fixed video targets; current configuration does not prove the historical destination throughout the selected dates. destinationAvailability=unavailable preserves analytics without inventing a destination. ab_tests: source (vidiq: saved results; youtube_studio: read for this request), totalExperiments, experiments (newest first, up to 25 unless videoIds are given) with videoId, title, testType, status (running, winner or completed), result (winner, inconclusive, notEnoughData or null), startedAt, endedAt and variants (label, title or thumbnail, watchTimeSharePercent, isWinner, isLeader, isApplied), plus videosWithoutTests for requested videos confirmed without a current test. notAccessible lists videos Studio did not return. complete and truncated describe coverage; stale marks an old saved answer. A missing saved test is not proof no test exists. search_suggestions: query, language, country (null means the country the browser is in), requestCount, partial and suggestions without duplicates: those for the query itself first, in YouTube's order, then the expansions' suggestions rank by rank. Each has text, rank (its position in YouTube's list for the request that returned it), source (seed for the query itself; letter, question or preposition for the query with modifier added) and modifier. They carry no search volume or competition. Follow and relay notes.

recovery.description: When present, show the user the action link and recovery steps. Wait for them to finish, then retry the original report parameters without the failed jobId. Do not automatically retry while disconnected.

name: vidiq_connect_extension
title: Connect vidIQ extension
description:
Show the user how to install, reconnect or update the vidIQ browser extension, which vidiq_channel_analytics_extended reads YouTube Studio through. Call it with the same report when vidiq_channel_analytics_extended returns extension_not_connected, or when the user asks how to connect the extension. The widget shows the link, steps and a Continue button and checks the connection itself: reply in one short sentence without repeating the steps, and wait for the user to finish. When the user then says the extension is connected, the card has already confirmed it, so do not call this tool again. When they ask you to check it (or press Retry report on an older card), call this tool again first. Only retry a previously requested Studio report when the extension is connected and all required parameters are known, preserving the original parameters. thumbnail_ctr requires 1–50 videoIds, startDate and an exclusive endDate. There is no whole-channel thumbnail CTR mode without video IDs. Ask for the missing videos and dates before calling the report; never invent them. If there is no earlier report request or required details are missing, ask the user before calling vidiq_channel_analytics_extended; opening this connection card alone is not a report request. Without a widget, show the returned link and steps. Free; reads no Studio data.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

report.description: The vidiq_channel_analytics_extended report the user asked for, so the card can tell whether the extension needs an update.

status.description: connection_required: no browser with the extension is connected. update_required: the connected extension is too old for the report. connected: a browser is connected now; retry the original report.

report.description: The report this check was for, so the card re-checks the same one.

recovery.description: The link and steps the widget shows. Without a widget, show the link and steps to the user.

name: vidiq_find_broll
title: Find Stock B-roll
description:
Find free stock B-roll video clips.

Provide a search query (optionally orientation and min/max duration filters).
Returns up to 4 clips with a direct mp4 link, a preview image, dimensions, and the
photographer credit. Attribution is required: always credit the photographer and
link back to the source page when using a clip.

Cost: 1 credit(s) per call.

query.description: Search term for the stock B-roll footage, e.g. 'city skyline at night'.

orientation.description: Optional orientation filter. Use 'portrait' for Shorts/Reels, 'landscape' otherwise.

minDurationSeconds.description: Optional minimum clip duration in seconds.

maxDurationSeconds.description: Optional maximum clip duration in seconds.

name: vidiq_voiceover_list_voices
title: List Voiceover Voices
description:
List the available voiceover voices.

Returns each voice's id, name, category, description, and an optional audio preview URL.
The user's own cloned/designed voices have isCustom=true and are listed first; prefer
them when the user asks for "my voice". Use the returned voiceId with vidiq_voiceover_generate.
Pass language (the script's two-letter code, e.g. "es"): the list then has every voice native to
that language, with descriptions and previews. Without it, voices of other languages are listed
in short form and not necessarily all of them, so call again with language before choosing one
for a script that is not in English. Choose by each voice's
`language` field, not by its place in the list: prefer a voice whose language matches the
script, since a voice carries its native accent into other languages, and use accent and gender
to tell matching voices apart. When none matches, any voice can read the script.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

language.description: Language of the script to narrate, as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code: Spanish script → "es".

sampleText.description: The first sentence or two of the script to narrate, copied exactly, when you already have the script. Where the app shows a voice picker, the user can then hear their own words in a voice before choosing it. Omit it when there is no script yet.

message.description: Present where the user is shown these voices in a picker: who chooses the voice, and what to do next.

voiceId.description: Opaque identifier to pass unchanged to vidiq_voiceover_generate. Do not modify or prefix it.

previewUrl.description: URL to an audio preview of the voice, if available.

language.description: The voice's native language as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code, when known.

accent.description: The voice's accent in its native language, when known.

isCustom.description: True if this is the user's own cloned/designed voice (listed first). Prefer these when the user refers to 'my voice'.

createdAt.description: When the user made this voice, for their own voices, when known.

voiceSource.description: How the user made this voice, for their own voices, when known.

name: vidiq_voiceover_generate
title: Generate Voiceover
description:
Generate a voiceover MP3 from a script.

Provide the script text (max 5000 characters) and a voiceId
from vidiq_voiceover_list_voices.

When a narration needs one audio file per line (one per scene, slide or caption),
pass every line at once in `scriptLines` (up to 50 lines, 5000
characters each, 20000 in total) instead of calling this tool once per line.
The result then has `lines`, with an `audioUrl` and `startSeconds` for each line, and
`audioUrl` is all lines joined in order. For a narration used as one piece, pass `script`.
Pass `script` or `scriptLines`, never both.

Narration over generated video clips (a voiceover or narrator, in any language) is made
here, once for the whole video, and never spoken in the clips' prompts: choose a voice native
to the script's language (vidiq_voiceover_list_voices with language), then pass the returned
`mcpJobId` to vidiq_compose as `voiceover.audioUrl` with the clips, rather than copying the
audio link. A clip speaks only lines a person in it says.

A short script usually finishes while this call waits: then `result` already
holds the audio duration, character count, and hosted MP3 URL, so do not poll.
Without `result`, poll `vidiq_job_poll` with the returned `mcpJobId` until it
is "completed". Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if
generation fails.

Cost: every 1,000 characters of script, or part of them, costs 28 credit(s): a script of up to 1,000 characters costs 28, one of 1,001 to 2,000 costs 56. The lines of scriptLines are charged together, on their combined length.

script.description: The text to synthesize into speech, as one piece. Omit it when passing scriptLines.

voiceId.description: Opaque voice identifier from vidiq_voiceover_list_voices. Copy it exactly as returned; do not modify or prefix it.

output.description: How to return the completed audio. 'url_only' (default) returns the hosted MP3 URL. 'url_and_audio' also attaches the MP3 inline when the terminal poll first completes.

scriptLines.description: The lines of a narration that needs one audio file per line, such as one per scene or caption. All lines are voiced in one job with the same voice, instead of one call per line. Omit it when passing script.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: 'inprogress' on every start result, whether or not the voiceover has finished. A present `result` means it is finished.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

result.description: Present when the voiceover finished while this call waited: durationSeconds, charCount and audioUrl (with scriptLines, all lines joined in order), as `vidiq_job_poll` returns them. With scriptLines it also has `lines`, one entry per line in order: index, audioUrl (that line alone), startSeconds (where it starts in the joined audioUrl), durationSeconds and charCount.

name: vidiq_generate_music
title: Generate Music
description:
Generate ONE original, royalty-free music track (MP3) from a text prompt: background music, or a song with vocals.

Describe the music in the prompt (max 3000 characters): genre + mood +
instrumentation + tempo works best. For background music with nobody singing, set instrumental.
For a song with given words, pass the words in lyrics and keep every direction in the prompt (max
2989 characters for the two together). Set durationSeconds (10-180) either way:
an instrumental track keeps to that length, a song aims for it.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll`
with that id until it is "completed" to get the actual audio duration and a permanent
download URL for the MP3. Rendering can take a couple of minutes for longer tracks.

Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if generation fails. If the
provider's safety filter blocks the prompt (this routinely happens to ordinary prompts),
the poll reports it with guidance to rephrase — suggest ONE rephrased prompt to the user
and wait for their agreement before calling again.

Cost: 25 credit(s) per generated track.

prompt.description: How the music should sound. Best results follow: [genre/style] + [mood] + [instrumentation] + [tempo/rhythm] + [vocal style & language]. For music with nobody singing, set `instrumental`. Words to be sung go in `lyrics`, not here; to have the words written for you, describe the theme here. Do NOT use negative phrasing (e.g. 'no drums') — it is not supported; describe what you want instead. Never ask for a breath, pause, gap or space between lines: the singer says the word aloud. Set the pace instead (tempo, one line per bar).

lyrics.description: The exact words to sing, in order, one sung line per line. Everything here is sung, so give only the words: no singer names, timings, notes or directions. A section tag on its own line ([Verse], [Chorus], [Bridge]) is fine, and words in parentheses are sung as backing vocals. The longest song (3 minutes) holds about 50 lines; more than fits is left unsung.

instrumental.description: True for music with nobody singing (background music). The track then keeps to durationSeconds: a render that runs long is cut to it and faded out. Leave out for a song.

durationSeconds.description: Length in seconds (10-180, default 30). Set it for a song too: the song aims for it and can run somewhat over or under, so read the returned durationSeconds. An instrumental track keeps to this length.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.
